item.title: Star RB Fluff Bothwell returning to Mississippi in 2027 with Kamario Taylor
item.description: Wesley Hale-Imagn Images Star RB Fluff Bothwell returning to Mississippi in 2027 with Kamario Taylor appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . Mississippi State had an amazing start to the season. They opened up 4-0, which included wins over Minnesota, South Carolina, and Missouri. Then, the injuries started to pile up. Star quarterback Kamario Taylor was lost for the season, and running back Fluff Bothwell also missed time. As the team sits at 4-6, plans are already being made for the 2027 campaign. Taylor has already comitted to returning to the Bulldogs next year. Now, Bothwell has decided to join him , according to a statement released by the running back through the school on social media. “Choosing Mississippi State was the best decision I’ve ever made. I came here to play in the best offensive scheme in college football – a running back’s dream. I also came to grow as a player and as a man, and to represent the maroon and white like all the greats before us. That’s why, every day, I’m going to keep fighting for Mississippi State alongside my coaches and teammates to make the entire Bulldog Family proud. Thanks to Coach Lebby and Coach Tucker for believing in me! I’m ALL IN on this program. We’re focused on these last two games, then going straight to work on a big 2027. Hail State!” the statement read. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) Bothwell was lightly recruited in the class of 2024. He was a three-star recruit, sitting at the 127th running back in the class. This led to his commitment to South Alabama. He broke out immediately in 2024, running for 832 yards and 13 touchdowns. Bothwell then hit the transfer portal and joined Mississippi State last season. In his first season with the Bulldogs, he ran for 677 yards and six touchdowns. This year, he has run for 649 yards and three scores, while also having 157 yards receiving and a touchdown. This is while dealing with injuries. He ran the ball just one time against Alabama before being hurt, and then missed the next game. It is of note the thank you to Jeff Lebby. The Mississippi State coach is in his third season as the head coach. The six-game skid for the Bulldogs, along with the fact that they could miss a bowl, has led to speculation that Lebby is on the hot seat at Mississippi State . With both Taylor and Bothwell committing to 2027, and Bothwell specifically calling out Lebby, the university may be keeping the coach to keep the players. item.title: Burna Boy, Asake, Seyi Vibez feature on GTA VI soundtrack
item.description: By Enitan Abdultawab Nigerian music stars Burna Boy, Asake and Seyi Vibez have secured spots on the soundtrack of the highly anticipated video game, Grand Theft Auto VI (GTA VI). The Nigerian artistes are among several international performers featured on the game’s soundtrack, which was recently unveiled by Rockstar Games, the developer of the popular gaming franchise. Some of their songs will feature on AfroBank FM, an in-game radio station dedicated to African music, including Afrobeats, amapiano, African classics and 3-step sounds. Burna Boy is also set to co-host the station alongside British DJ and record producer Palms Trax, who appears in the game under the name Palmsy. Among the Nigerian tracks featured on the station are Asake’s ‘Joha’ and ‘Giza’, a collaboration between Burna Boy and Seyi Vibez. The station’s previewed playlist also includes ‘Gye Wani’ by Pat Thomas featuring Ebo Taylor, as well as ‘Shay’sana’ by DJ Lag and Robot Boii featuring Kamo Mphela. Burna Boy also makes a separate contribution to the game’s official soundtrack with his song ‘Bigger’. Other international artistes featured on the soundtrack include Travis Scott, Dua Lipa, Cardi B, Gunna, Young Thug, Kodak Black, Don Toliver, Zara Larsson, Camila Cabello and Lana Del Rey. The development marks another international gaming appearance for Nigerian music, as Afrobeats continues to gain visibility across global entertainment platforms. GTA VI is the latest instalment in Rockstar Games’ Grand Theft Auto series, one of the world’s most popular video game franchises. The post Burna Boy, Asake, Seyi Vibez feature on GTA VI soundtrack appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: Voyager 1 celebrates one light-day with a nice lie-down
item.description: Voyager 1 marked its milestone of one light-day from Earth in time-honored fashion: by giving controllers the silent treatment. On November 14, the mission team noticed that the veteran spacecraft had stopped returning science and engineering data. A Deep Space Network antenna in Canberra, Australia, picked up its carrier signal, but no data. The carrier signal indicates that Voyager 1 can still keep its antenna pointed at Earth and operate its transmitting equipment. However, something could be amiss with the system responsible for collecting and collating data from the spacecraft. Something similar happened in 2023 . After a few months of troubleshooting, engineers managed to coax a response from the probe, and by June 2024, NASA was delighted to announce that the spacecraft was back in action. The problem was traced to a faulty computer chip, and engineers devised a software update to work around the defective hardware. That experience will stand the team in good stead this time around. There was also a brief interruption in communications with Voyager 1 in October, which could have been caused by the spacecraft dropping into safe mode after a thruster failover occurred. Engineers are investigating whether the two incidents are connected. The Voyagers have an impressive amount of fault protection built in, which has contributed to their extraordinary longevity. It will be half a century in 2027 since the spacecraft were launched, so glitches are understandable and likely. NASA expects to confirm on November 19 that Voyager 1 was still operating when it reached one light-day from Earth on November 18, using its carrier signal and trajectory calculations. The day's delay neatly illustrates a major headache for engineers: communication latency. It now takes more than 24 hours for commands to reach the spacecraft, and the same amount of time for a response to be received. Diagnosing the fault could therefore take weeks or longer. ®

item.title: LaMelo Ball Isn’t Buying the Story About His Defense
item.description: IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect LaMelo Ball had just helped rescue the Timberwolves with his defense when a reporter asked whether he was playing the best defense of his career. The question fit the finish. Ball’s deflection of a Portland inbound pass had created the possession that ended with Jaden McDaniels scoring the winning basket. He also contested the Trail Blazers’ final shot as Minnesota held on for a 106-105 victory Tuesday. Ball’s answer, however, challenged the premise. “Honestly, I feel like I’m doing the same I’ve been doing,” he said in the locker room . “Maybe just more highlighted, I guess.” LaMelo Ball clutch steal + Jaden McDaniels transition layup WOW pic.twitter.com/ErQS4JFr66 — Wolves Videos (@WolvesVids) November 18, 2026 It was a different interpretation from the idea that Minnesota has unlocked an entirely new defensive version of its point guard. Ball sees continuity in his effort, with greater attention now being paid to those contributions. His coach sees a player helping the Wolves win even while his scoring rhythm has become harder to find. “He’s still competing. He’s still guarding. He’s still rebounding,” Chris Finch said afterward . Nov 2, 2026; Minneapolis, Minnesota, USA; Minnesota Timberwolves center Rudy Gobert (27) and guard LaMelo Ball (1) enjoy a moment after a break from action with the Milwaukee Bucks in the fourth quarter at Target Center. Mandatory Credit: Bruce Kluckhohn-Imagn Images Tuesday required all of it. Ball finished with 18 points on 7-of-17 shooting and grabbed 10 rebounds. But his most important contribution came after an offensive possession that could have left Minnesota with little chance to recover. Trailing by one, Ball attempted a difficult jumper that missed with 9.5 seconds remaining. He believed there had been contact. The whistle never came, and Portland had possession with an opportunity to protect its lead. Ball acknowledged afterward that he had been seeking the call. “I know it was a bad play before. I was looking for a foul,” he said. “So I knew we had to get the ball back or just make something happen.” After Minnesota used its foul to give, Ball disrupted Donovan Clingan’s inbound pass toward Jrue Holiday. Ayo Dosunmu gathered the loose ball and pushed up the floor before finding McDaniels for the go-ahead layup with 2.6 seconds left. The Wolves still needed to defend. Oct 23, 2026; Orlando, Florida, USA; Minnesota Timberwolves guard LaMelo Ball (1) controls the ball from Orlando Magic guard Jalen Suggs (4) in the fourth quarter at Kia Center. Mandatory Credit: Nathan Ray Seebeck-Imagn Images Trey Lyles blocked Damian Lillard’s ensuing attempt out of bounds. Officials restored one second to the clock, giving Portland another opportunity. Ball sees continuity in his effort, with greater attention now being paid to those contributions. His coach sees a player helping the Wolves win even while his scoring rhythm has become harder to find. “He’s still competing. He’s still guarding. He’s still rebounding,” Chris Finch said afterward . Nov 2, 2026; Minneapolis, Minnesota, USA; Minnesota Timberwolves center Rudy Gobert (27) and guard LaMelo Ball (1) enjoy a moment after a break from action with the Milwaukee Bucks in the fourth quarter at Target Center. Mandatory Credit: Bruce Kluckhohn-Imagn Images Tuesday required all of it. Ball finished with 18 points on 7-of-17 shooting and grabbed 10 rebounds. But his most important contribution came after an offensive possession that could have left Minnesota with little chance to recover. Trailing by one, Ball attempted a difficult jumper that missed with 9.5 seconds remaining. He believed there had been contact. The whistle never came, and Portland had possession with an opportunity to protect its lead. Ball acknowledged afterward that he had been seeking the call. “I know it was a bad play before. I was looking for a foul,” he said. “So I knew we had to get the ball back or just make something happen.” After Minnesota used its foul to give, Ball disrupted Donovan Clingan’s inbound pass toward Jrue Holiday. Ayo Dosunmu gathered the loose ball and pushed up the floor before finding McDaniels for the go-ahead layup with 2.6 seconds left. The Wolves still needed to defend. Oct 23, 2026; Orlando, Florida, USA; Minnesota Timberwolves guard LaMelo Ball (1) controls the ball from Orlando Magic guard Jalen Suggs (4) in the fourth quarter at Kia Center. Mandatory Credit: Nathan Ray Seebeck-Imagn Images Trey Lyles blocked Damian Lillard’s ensuing attempt out of bounds. Officials restored one second to the clock, giving Portland another opportunity. The final inbound sequence ended with Toumani Camara attempting a contested shot against Ball in the paint. Minnesota survived, and Ball had supplied two defensive interventions after missing the potential go-ahead jumper. For Dosunmu, that response was the important part. “That’s all about competing,” he noted. “You have to stay in the moment.” Dosunmu explained that he tries to encourage Ball through the frustration of missing shots he normally makes. The opportunity to influence the next possession remains, regardless of what happened on the previous one. “We don’t win that game if he don’t make that play,” Dosunmu told the media after the game. Finch also pointed out that Tuesday’s late steal was part of a pattern. He recalled Ball making another important steal to help secure the win in Houston earlier this month. “We love that part about him,” Finch said. “He’s really embraced that here.” Nov 17, 2026; Minneapolis, Minnesota, USA; Minnesota Timberwolves guard LaMelo Ball (1) celebrates as Portland Trail Blazers center Donovan Clingan (23) looks on at Target Center. Mandatory Credit: Jesse Johnson-Imagn Images That assessment can coexist with Ball’s view of his own history. His postgame answer was a personal evaluation, rather than proof that his defensive performance has remained identical across teams and seasons. Establishing that would require more than one dramatic finish. What Tuesday demonstrated was his ability to remain involved when the offensive end became frustrating. The 10 rebounds helped Minnesota recover possessions. His activity on the inbound pass created the winning opportunity. His final contest helped close the game. Ball can debate whether those contributions represent a change or simply greater recognition. The Timberwolves will gladly keep taking them. “Got to get the ball back, do something to win,” he said of his thinking after the missed jumper. On Tuesday, he did exactly that. item.title: ‘Ya’ll know the price’: Floyd Schofield Sr calls out Abdullah Mason’s team over ‘lowball offer’
item.description: There’s been some initial talks of a potential meeting between Floyd ‘Kid Austin’ Schofield and Abdullah Mason but it would seem things aren’t going so smoothly as the sides are apparently far apart on the money. During a recent social media post Schofield’s father, Floyd Schofield Sr , would call out Mason’s team for what they say was an insulting offer for the fight. “How ya’ll going to send us a lowball offer,” Schofield Sr would say. “Isn’t that some bullsh-t. That is so Mason. Anyway, ya’ll know we ain’t taking no $700,000. Come on, now. Ya’ll know the offer is $2.5M, that’s the offer, period. That’s it. Make that happen so we can fight. All this ‘we’ll give you a million, you bring home $700,000’, nah. Ya’ll know the price. “We ain’t even going to fool the fans. Either ya’ll ready to fight or ya’ll had a purse to fight or ya’ll don’t and we go on to Rayo [Valenzuela] and we do what we got to do. Don’t waste our time with no bull crap offers. $2.5M at least, and that’s it. Ya’ll already knew that before you sent that bogus offer.” Based strictly on what Sr says here, they are seeking more than twice the amount of money than has been offered thus far, and that would appear to be a wide gulf to bridge considering the actual economics of a matchup of this kind, considering neither fighter is a particularly huge draw. That being the case, this proposed fight could be dead in the water in the early going.

item.title: Perfect Week 11 NFL DFS DraftKings Showdown Lineup for Thursday Night Football Features Nico Collins
item.description: Houston Texans wide receiver Nico Collins (12) reacts after a catch against Cleveland Browns cornerback Denzel Ward (21) during the second quarter at Huntington Bank Field. | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect The Indianapolis Colts are set to face the Houston Texans on Thursday Night Football to get Week 11 underway. In a battle between two disappointing AFC South teams on Thursday, Nico Collins stands out against the Colts. Showdown is a single-game DFS contest on DraftKings, where you'll have a $50,000 salary to select a captain and five flex players to complete your roster. The captain's salary and points are multiplied by 1.5x, while the flex players' salaries and points are normal. With that in mind, which players build a perfect showdown lineup between the Colts and Texans? All stats used in this article are from PFF or Sumer Sports unless stated otherwise. DraftKings uses full-PPR scoring in their DFS contests, so keep that in mind when making lineups. Nico Collins, WR, Houston Texans ($15,300 Salary) Houston Texans wide receiver Nico Collins (12) celebrates after a touchdown during the first quarter against the Cleveland Browns at Huntington Bank Field. | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Collins is averaging the most DraftKings points per game (17.0) among the non-QBs in Thursday's contest. After earning a season-low 4 targets in Week 9, Collins caught 9 of his season-high 16 targets for 94 yards and a score en route to 24.4 DraftKings points in Week 10. Of the 115 WRs with 100-plus routes run this season, Collins has the 19th-highest target share (24.0%) and the 22nd most yards per route run (2.15). C.J. Stroud, QB, Houston Texans ($10,000 Salary) Houston Texans quarterback C.J. Stroud (7) scrambles during the second quarter against the Cleveland Browns at Huntington Bank Field. | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect C.J. Stroud is producing a slate-high 22.4 DraftKings points per game, and he's been a major positive on a disappointing Texans squad. Among the 29 QBs with 200-plus plays in 2026, Stroud has the 9th-most adjusted EPA/play (0.17) and the 13th-highest success rate (47.9%). The Colts' defense is coughing up the 12th-most schedule-adjusted fantasy points per game to QBs (+1.2). David Montgomery, RB, Houston Texans ($8,200 Salary) Houston Texans running back David Montgomery (32) rushes against the Dallas Cowboys at Reliant Stadium. | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Woody Marks has been ruled out for the Texans on Thursday, but veteran David Montgomery is expected to return after a four-game absence. Although Montgomery was ineffective following a 28.9-point outing in Week 1, he can excel against a below-average Indy run defense. Entering Week 11, the Colts' defense is permitting the third-most schedule-adjusted fantasy points per game to RBs (+4.6). Tank Dell, WR, Houston Texans ($6,400 Salary) Houston Texans wide receiver Tank Dell (1) runs onto the field before the game against the New York Giants at Reliant Stadium. | IMAGN IMAG

With Marvin Harrison Jr. inactive again in Week 11, Dell should see a healthy amount of snaps against the Colts. While Dell is a boom-or-bust option, his 21.1 yards per reception gives him plenty of upside against a shaky Indy secondary. Spencer Shrader, K, Indianapolis Colts ($5,200 Salary) Indianapolis Colts kicker Spencer Shrader (3) kicks a field goal during the third quarter against the Dallas Cowboys at Lucas Oil Stadium. | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect The Colts have struggled to generate points consistently, but kicker Spencer Shrader is notching a solid 11.4 DraftKings points per game. Shrader has converted 23 of his 25 field-goal attempts, and he's recorded 14-plus DraftKings points in 5 of his first 10 contests this season. When Indianapolis took on Houston in Week 3, Shrader posted 17 DraftKings points with 4 field goals and an extra point. Seth McGowan, RB, Indianapolis Colts ($4,600 Salary) Indianapolis Colts running back Seth McGowan (20) rushes the ball against the Miami Dolphins in the second half at Lucas Oil Stadium. | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Even with Jonathan Taylor staying on the Colts past the trade deadline, rookie Seth McGowan is still garnering a decent workload. McGowan has accrued 11-plus DraftKings points in back-to-back games, and he earned a season-high 12 rushing attempts in Week 10. The Texans' defense is allowing the 13th-most schedule-adjusted fantasy points per game to RBs (+0.8). item.title: What to know about Xi, Putin and Trump's historic trilateral summit
item.description: China's Xi Jinping, Russian President Vladimir Putin and his US counterpart Donald Trump met for a historic summit in Shenzhen, China, on Thursday, where they agreed on a "peace declaration". The three leaders pledged to reform the UN, increase supplies of refined petroleum products and uphold the immunity enjoyed by officials in international courts.

item.title: UDUS medical academics threaten five-day warning strike
item.description: By Musa Ubandawaki, Sokoto The Nigerian Association of Medical and Dental Academics (NAMDA), Usmanu Danfodiyo University, Sokoto (UDUS)/Usmanu Danfodiyo University Teaching Hospital (UDUTH) Chapter, has threatened to embark on a five-day warning strike over alleged irregularities in salary payments, partial implementation of professional allowances and outstanding promotion arrears owed to its members. The association, at a press briefing in Sokoto on Thursday, said the unresolved welfare and remuneration issues had persisted despite several rounds of consultations, formal correspondence and peaceful engagements with the university management. It warned that its members might be left with no option but to embark on an indefinite strike if the issues were not addressed. Speaking at the briefing, presided over by Professor Usman Bello, NAMDA said its members had exercised considerable patience and goodwill through sustained dialogue with the relevant authorities, but expressed regret that the engagements had not produced the desired results. The association said its concerns centred on the continued partial implementation of professional allowances under the revised Consolidated Medical Salary Structure (CONMESS), unexplained salary disparities among members on the same grade levels and steps, and the non-payment of promotion arrears covering 2017 to 2024. It also alleged that some eligible members were excluded from the payment of 2025 and 2026 promotion arrears, describing the situation as an administrative and financial burden that had continued to affect the welfare and morale of medical academics. According to the association, comparable institutions in both Northern and Southern Nigeria had fully implemented the revised CONMESS, a development it said had heightened concerns among its members over disparities in remuneration. NAMDA recalled that it had pursued several avenues to resolve the dispute, including meetings with university authorities, submission of formal letters and supporting documents, and interventions by senior colleagues and elders. However, it said those efforts had yet to yield the desired outcome. item.content:encoded: By Musa Ubandawaki, Sokoto The Nigerian Association of Medical and Dental Academics (NAMDA), Usmanu Danfodiyo University, Sokoto (UDUS)/Usmanu Danfodiyo University Teaching Hospital (UDUTH) Chapter, has threatened to embark on a five-day warning strike over alleged irregularities in salary payments, partial implementation of professional allowances and outstanding promotion arrears owed to its members. The association, at a press briefing in Sokoto on Thursday, said the unresolved welfare and remuneration issues had persisted despite several rounds of consultations, formal correspondence and peaceful engagements with the university management. It warned that its members might be left with no option but to embark on an indefinite strike if the issues were not addressed. Speaking at the briefing, presided over by Professor Usman Bello, NAMDA said its members had exercised considerable patience and goodwill through sustained dialogue with the relevant authorities, but expressed regret that the engagements had not produced the desired results. The association said its concerns centred on the continued partial implementation of professional allowances under the revised Consolidated Medical Salary Structure (CONMESS), unexplained salary disparities among members on the same grade levels and steps, and the non-payment of promotion arrears covering 2017 to 2024. It also alleged that some eligible members were excluded from the payment of 2025 and 2026 promotion arrears, describing the situation as an administrative and financial burden that had continued to affect the welfare and morale of medical academics. According to the association, comparable institutions in both Northern and Southern Nigeria had fully implemented the revised CONMESS, a development it said had heightened concerns among its members over disparities in remuneration. NAMDA recalled that it had pursued several avenues to resolve the dispute, including meetings with university authorities, submission of formal letters and supporting documents, and interventions by senior colleagues and elders. However, it said those efforts had yet to yield the desired outcome. The association also raised concerns over the migration of experienced medical professionals, including senior consultants and professors, to other countries in search of better working conditions. It described the development, popularly known as “japa”, as a threat to medical education and healthcare delivery in the country. “Mr President is aware of the ongoing exodus of highly experienced academic staff, including senior consultants and professors, to other countries, a trend popularly known as ‘japa’,” it said. NAMDA added that the Federal Government’s decision to increase the admission quota for medical students had placed additional pressure on the declining number of medical teachers. It warned that increasing student intake without corresponding investment in recruiting and retaining qualified medical lecturers could undermine the quality of medical education. The association said medical teachers, under NAMDA, the Medical and Dental Consultants Association of Nigeria (MDCAN) and the Nigerian Medical Association (NMA), had continued to discharge their responsibilities despite the challenges. “Despite these challenges, medical teachers have continued to impart knowledge and skills without compromising quality or professional standards,” it said. NAMDA further disclosed that the Minister of Education had directed vice-chancellors to ensure the payment of outstanding arrears owed to medical teachers in compliance with a presidential directive. It said several other universities had implemented the directive, but alleged that the management of UDUS had yet to act on it despite sustained engagements. The association said its congress had consequently resolved to issue a 21-day ultimatum to the university management, effective November 3, 2026, demanding the resolution of all outstanding welfare and remuneration issues before the notice expires on November 24. It warned that failure to address the concerns would trigger a five-day warning strike. “Should these concerns remain unaddressed at the expiry of the notice on Tuesday, November 24, 2026, members shall commence a five-day warning strike from 12 midnight on Wednesday, November 25, 2026,” it stated. The association added that it would review the situation after the warning strike, including the possibility of embarking on an indefinite industrial action if the dispute remained unresolved. Despite the planned action, NAMDA appealed for urgent intervention and constructive engagement, saying it remained willing to work with the university management towards a lasting resolution in the interest of medical academics, students and patients who depend on the institution’s services. item.title: Lauren Price and the three fights that could take women’s boxing to a new level in 2027
item.description: Lauren Price is the No 1 welterweight boxer in the world, she fights on BBC television, she is unbeaten, she has an Olympic gold medal, and all she wants is a big fight. It is what she deserves. Price defends her world titles on Friday night in Cardiff when she meets Austria’s Michaela Kotaskova over the 10-round championship distance, in a fight that will be shown live on BBC 2. It is a perfectly good fight against a decent, proven opponent, but Price has her sights set firmly on one of the sport’s big names. During the last year, various boxers have been linked with Price; deals have been reached, with fights close to being made, and then the contests have collapsed. It is not unusual, but it is frustrating. In theory, there is still an active plan to fight the world’s No 1 female fighter Claressa Shields in America. Shields is unbeaten in 19 fights, has won world titles at four different weights, and is desperate for a test. She also won gold medals in back-to-back Olympics at Price’s weight. “I think the problem was the rematch clause,” said Price. “Shields didn’t want to come to Cardiff. I had no problem going to America to fight her, but she was not too keen on coming back here.” Chantelle Cameron (right) and Mikaela Mayer clashed in August and will do so again in December (Getty) So far in 2026, Shields has defended both her middleweight and heavyweight world titles – she weighed only 174lb for her heavyweight defence in February – and just two weeks ago she was locked in negotiations for a fight with Northampton super-welterweight Chantelle Cameron . However, Cameron has just announced that she will have a rematch with Las Vegas-based Mikaela Mayer on Christmas Eve in Dubai . They met in August in Birmingham , and Cameron won a wafer-thin decision in defence of her super-welterweight title, taking two belts from Mayer in the process. Price would also benefit from a fight with either Cameron or Mayer. In either fight, there would be no weight hazards, whereas a fight against Shields would inevitably mean that Price, who weighs 147lb naturally, would be conceding considerable poundage. Mayer has gained nearly 20lb from her original weight to fight the bigger women and make more money ; the women’s game is a fluid business, and sometimes the price is right when the weight is wrong. Price is an Olympic gold medalist and is unbeaten as a professional (Getty) “I have given away weight for years in the amateurs,” Price added. “I did it when I won my Olympic medal; I was never a full middleweight, never even close to the limit, but there was no Olympic weight for me at my natural weight, so I had no option.” Shields, who is just one year younger than Price at 31, did weigh 159lb in August when she last defended her middleweight title. Price is an Olympic gold medalist and is unbeaten as a professional (Getty) “I have given away weight for years in the amateurs,” Price added. “I did it when I won my Olympic medal; I was never a full middleweight, never even close to the limit, but there was no Olympic weight for me at my natural weight, so I had no option.” Shields, who is just one year younger than Price at 31, did weigh 159lb in August when she last defended her middleweight title. On Friday night, Price will have her eyes fixed firmly on Kotaskova, but no doubt she will want one of the three other women next year in a fight that she deserves – and a fight that boxing needs. Price vs Shields is exactly that bout, and a date next April would be fantastic.

item.title: TT 2027 Sidecar regulations amended
item.description: TT organisers say they recognise the changes may mean a "smaller field" next year [BBC] New rules for the Sidecar class at TT 2027 have dropped requirements for the likes of bodywork, fairings and aerodynamics, but teams are still required to switch to Sportbike engines and electronic control systems. The rules, implemented following a review of the future of sidecars at the races, were revised after feedback from competitors and teams about the cost and time available to make the necessary changes. In June, the class was suspended on safety grounds. Rules introduced last week led to the withdrawal of three teams and prompted race organisers to review their plans. On Wednesday, the racing body said the new measures which have now been decided upon were central to delivering "the significant and controllable" reduction in speed which was required for the return of the class for 2027 and beyond. "We recognise from the outset the time, investment and practical undertaking required of competitors and teams to adapt to the new regulations - and that initially the field will be smaller," organisers said. The effectiveness of the changes would be reviewed during and after TT 2027, they added, "taking account of incident evidence, speeds and machinery performance, technical compliance and reliability, competitor feedback, specialist technical input and the amount of qualifying and racing completed". Organisers said the class had an "established place" in the history of the event and "the responsibility now is to make changes, and create the conditions so it can continue and develop over the longer term". Two races are confirmed to take place around the Mountain Course in June next year. Read more stories from the Isle of Man on the BBC, watch BBC North West Tonight on BBC iPlayer and follow BBC Isle of Man on Facebook and X . item.title: Luka Doncic Has Priceless Reaction To Referee Being Held Back During Heated Exchange
item.description: Mandatory Credit: Jayne Kamin-Oncea-Imagn Images Luka Doncic looked absolutely stunned after referee Tre Maddox stepped toward him during a heated exchange at halftime of the Los Angeles Lakers ‘ 109-97 loss to the Utah Jazz on Wednesday. Lakers assistant coach Scott Brooks intervened and pushed Maddox away, which left Doncic just staring at the official with a puzzled expression as teammates tried to push him toward the locker room to avoid any further escalation. The confrontation began after Luka just barely missed a half-court shot, and the players started leaving the floor. Luka appeared to tell Maddox something before Maddox stepped in and appeared to ask Doncic, “What did you say?” The referee Tre Maddox actually tries to square up against Luka Doncic, after Luka said something to him, leaving Luka perplexed. Luka nearly hit the 3/4 court shot to end the 1st half — MrBuckBuck (@MrBuckBuckNBA) November 19, 2026 That was before Scott Brooks positioned himself between them. Maddox initially had a confrontational look on his face but later calmed down and eventually made his way back to the locker room. Austin Reaves and Matisse Thybulle were also nearby, and they made sure that Luka did not escalate any further. What Doncic actually said to prompt that kind of reaction from Maddox is still very unclear, and we might never know it. Luka’s expression was definitely the highlight of the clip. He continued to look toward Maddox as Brooks walked the referee away in the opposite direction, seemingly trying to process what had just happened. This was quite an unusual sight, as a coach stepped in front of an official to stop an argument with a player, which is very rare to see. Luka is generally the animated one whenever he disagrees with a call. In this instance, though, his relatively restrained reaction actually stood out. He didn’t follow Maddox or try to get around the people separating them or even try to get into the conversation again. Brooks’ intervention eventually allowed both men to leave the exchange without it becoming a bigger incident. The footage does show a tense confrontation, but it doesn’t establish what Maddox intended to do or the full conversation that preceded it. This was not the only viral clip of Luka arguing with officials from this game. In another clip, he is walking away after speaking with another official, Danica Barrody, and he appeared to mouth, “She’s so bad.” Luka and the female ref are going AT IT Ref: “You need to stop, just stop.” Luka: “She’s so bad!” — BrickCenter (@BrickCenter_) November 19, 2026 Although some reports described a technical foul against Doncic, which would have been his 2nd of the season, the game’s box score lists the technical foul as a bench technical. item.content:encoded: Mandatory Credit: Jayne Kamin-Oncea-Imagn Images Luka Doncic looked absolutely stunned after referee Tre Maddox stepped toward him during a heated exchange at halftime of the Los Angeles Lakers ‘ 109-97 loss to the Utah Jazz on Wednesday. Lakers assistant coach Scott Brooks intervened and pushed Maddox away, which left Doncic just staring at the official with a puzzled expression as teammates tried to push him toward the locker room to avoid any further escalation. The confrontation began after Luka just barely missed a half-court shot, and the players started leaving the floor. Luka appeared to tell Maddox something before Maddox stepped in and appeared to ask Doncic, “What did you say?” The referee Tre Maddox actually tries to square up against Luka Doncic, after Luka said something to him, leaving Luka perplexed. Luka nearly hit the 3/4 court shot to end the 1st half — MrBuckBuck (@MrBuckBuckNBA) November 19, 2026 That was before Scott Brooks positioned himself between them. Maddox initially had a confrontational look on his face but later calmed down and eventually made his way back to the locker room. Brooks’ intervention eventually allowed both men to leave the exchange without it becoming a bigger incident. This was not the only viral clip of Luka arguing with officials from this game. In another clip, he is walking away after speaking with another official, Danica Barrody, and he appeared to mouth, “She’s so bad.” Luka and the female ref are going AT IT Ref: “You need to stop, just stop.” Luka: “She’s so bad!” — BrickCenter (@BrickCenter_) November 19, 2026 Although some reports described a technical foul against Doncic, which would have been his 2nd of the season, the game’s box score lists the technical foul as a bench technical. Utah led 56-54 at halftime and eventually pulled away with a 15-0 fourth-quarter run. Keyonte George finished with 30 points and 10 assists, while Doncic scored 29 points with five rebounds and seven assists . His production came with significant problems: He shot 10-of-28 from the field, missed 10 of his 12 three-point attempts, and committed nine turnovers. After the game, Luka put the entire blame on himself, saying that he needs to do a lot better. “Yeah, honestly, I just have to do way better than this. This is unacceptable on my part. I have to lead the team better. As I said, I just have to look at this game, move on, and learn from it…. Well, just a little bit of everything. Obviously, the shots and the turnovers. Those two are specific. I think defensively we’re in a good place. Offensively, I have to lead the team better than this.” The defeat ended the Lakers’ nine-game winning streak and left them at 13-3. They shot season lows of 38.2% from the field and 27.3% from three-point range as they continued to play without an injured Austin Reaves. Doncic’s stare at Maddox made for a very memorable clip, but his postgame response spoke volumes about the loss. Whatever his frustration was with the officials, the Lakers needed better shooting and fewer mistakes from their leading scorer. Luka took the blame himself rather than making the confrontation the explanation for the loss, which would have sounded like an excuse.

item.title: Free Agent Poll: Adrián Morejón
item.description: MILWAUKEE, WISCONSIN - OCTOBER 03: Adrian Morejon #50 of the San Diego Padres pitches against the Milwaukee Brewers during the seventh inning in game one of the National League Division Series at American Family Field on October 03, 2026 in Milwaukee, Wisconsin. (Photo by Patrick McDermott/Getty Images) | Getty Images We have been doing this for a few years now: looking at the top free agents, using the contract Ben Clemens suggests he’ll get, and asking whether you would like the Jays to give him that contract. This year, the lockout makes it a little more complicated. Keith Law’s list is here . Ben Clemens’ is here. Adrián Morejón is number 8 on Ben Clemens list and number 19 on Keith Law’s. Morejón is a left-handed reliever. He’s 27, 28 at the end of February, young for a free agent.. He’s pitched eight seasons in the MLB, all for the Padres, but the first five of those he totaled just 50 games. But, in the last three, he’s pitched in 211 games, with a 2.58 ERA. In 223.1 inning he’s allowed 177 hits, 66 walks with 248 strikeouts and a 5.5 bWAR. He’s been one of the best relievers in the game. Baseball Savant says he’s in the 99th percentile in expected ERA, 98th in Fastball Velocity and 99th in Chase Rate. He’s also been 98th in Ground Ball % and 99th in Barrel %. His sinker averaged in 99.5 mph and his four seamer 99.3 mph last year. Keith Law said: By fWAR, Morejon is the best reliever available in free agency this year, producing 2.8 fWAR across 86 innings with a 2.37 FIP that put him in the top 10 among all MLB relievers in 2026. The Cuban southpaw will pitch at age 28 next year, which also makes him one of the youngest free agents available. He held left-handed batters to a .180/.234/.227 line this year, and was still effective against righties, who hit .222/.307/.302 off him. He’s mostly sinker/changeup now, as he’s shelved the curveball he used in the minors. His slider has strong “shape” characteristics that should make it effective, but hitters disagree, hitting it harder than any of his other weapons this past year. He’s lowered his arm slot about 10 degrees over the past few seasons, which could be part of why he’s stayed healthy for three seasons after elbow and shoulder injuries afflicted him for several years before that. Ben figures he’ll get a three-year contract at $24 million per year for a total of $72 million.

item.title: Hammered: Worst Duke Losses Since 2020
item.description: DURHAM, NORTH CAROLINA - NOVEMBER 17: Patrick Ngongba II #21 of the Duke Blue Devils reacts after fouling out in the second half against the Illinois Fighting Illini during their game at Cameron Indoor Stadium on November 17, 2026 in Durham, North Carolina. (Photo by Jacob Kupferman/Getty Images) | Getty Images W hen things didn’t go well for Duke against Illinois the other night, the 99-78 loss at Iconic Cameron Indoor Stadium (“iconic” is de rigueur nowadays) was a bit of a shock. Jon Scheyer ’s talent rich Blue Devils don’t lose often, especially not at home. Duke usually ranks high in the polls, sometimes the only ACC team that’s sufficiently strong to merit national attention. When and if Duke loses we expect the action to be intense, the score to be close. The game against the Illini wasn’t close. Losing by only a few points feels different than falling by a double figure margin, which implies the victor was clearly dominant, even if only at game’s end. Under first Mike Krzyzewski and, most recently, Scheyer, the Devils have fallen by 11 points or more just 13 times in this decade, that is the 2019-20 season through Nov. 17, 2026. Last season Duke lost only three games – against Texas Tech at Madison Square Garden in December, at UNC in early February, and by a point against UConn in the Elite Eight. The three ’26 defeats were by a combined five points, making the size of the early Illinois defeat rather unexpected. The 21-point losing margin against the Illini was exceeded only three times since 2020. In fact, and here’s a real oddity, under former head coach Kevin Keatts NC State delivered more of Duke’s most decisive defeats than anyone else over the course of the last six-plus seasons. That includes the largest margin, 84-60 at Raleigh in 2023, and a stinging ejection from the 2024 NCAA Tournament. Illinois has twice decisively outmuscled the Blue Devils, in the early 2022 season and again in this one, both times under Brad Underwood. UNC also twice won against Duke by comfortable margins, in 2021 and 2022, under Hubert Davis. item.title: Wayne Gretzky sees no comparison between Connor McDavid & other NHL stars
item.description: Wayne Gretzky has said that Connor McDavid remains in a class of his own, with the Edmonton Oilers captain producing another remarkable season. After leading the league with 138 points last season, the Oilers captain has registered 55 points so far, including 13 goals and 42 assists with a plus-minus rating of 29. Speaking on NHL on TNT, Gretzky praised McDavid’s scoring pace, leadership, and determination to win the Stanley Cup. He also highlighted Leon Draisaitl and Evan Bouchard as important parts of Edmonton’s success. When Liam McHugh asked whether McDavid looked different this season, Gretzky offered a clear assessment. “Well, I think it’s a combination of things. First, he’s the best player in the game today, right? There’s no comparison,” Gretzky said. MORE: Oilers’ Mike Babcock explains decision to split Connor McDavid & Leon Draisaitl McDavid recently tied Gretzky with his 23rd consecutive game with a point to start a season. Gretzky owns the record with 51 games in 1983-84, while his 30-game streak from 1982-83 shares second place with Mats Sundin. Mario Lemieux also recorded a 46-game point streak during the 1989-90 season, although it did not begin the season. Wayne Gretzky credits Connor McDavid’s leadership Sunrise, Florida, USA; Edmonton Oilers center Connor McDavid (97) looks on at Amerant Bank Arena. Mandatory Credit: Sam Navarro-Imagn Images Credit: IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect (Reuters) Gretzky thinks McDavid’s pursuit of a championship has helped push the Oilers forward. “Secondly, I think it’s his drive to want to win a Stanley Cup. And winning a Stanley Cup starts in September,” Gretzky explained. “And his leadership, his work ethic and his commitment to the group and to the team.” Draisaitl has also delivered an outstanding campaign with 21 goals and 44 points, while Bouchard, with 37 points, has impressed on defense. Gretzky thinks Edmonton has improved defensively through better preparation and stronger commitment. “Leon Draisaitl has been incredible,” Gretzky said. “He’s having one of those years that’s just as good as close to anybody ever in hockey. And Bouchard on defense. I saw Connor say one day that he can’t believe that he didn’t win the Norris last year. Well, it’s going to be pretty tough for somebody to take it away from him this year… they’re a lot better team defensively right now. “… They don’t want to not be successful this year. You can see it on the best players’ face.” MORE: Oilers’ Connor McDavid points to goalie Devon Levi’s biggest strength after 8-1 start The Oilers’ 10-0 road record has also caught Gretzky’s attention. He called that achievement incredible given the competition across the NHL. Edmonton has reached the Stanley Cup Final in each of the past two seasons but failed to win the championship. Gretzky hopes McDavid can finally lead the franchise to the title. “They’re on a good stretch here. And I hope he breaks all my records,” Gretzky said. “He’s a tremendous young man. It’s good for

item.title: Why Jaguars’ Parker Washington Could Have a Monster Week 11 Against the Giants
item.description: Fantasy football managers who have Jacksonville Jaguars star wide receiver Parker Washington have a reason to feel excited about the prospect of him going off in Week 11. The Jaguars are scheduled to face the New York Giants this coming Sunday at MetLife Stadium in East Rutherford, and according to research from Next Gen Stats , it appears that this is a matchup that favors Washington in at least one particualrly intriguing way. “Parker Washington has averaged 5.0 yards per route against press coverage this season, the most in the NFL, ahead of Jaxon Smith-Njigba (4.7). The Giants’ defense has pressed at least one cornerback on 70.6% of their plays this season, the highest rate in the NFL,” the graphic that NFL Fantasy Football posted on X, formerly Twitter. The matchup looks particularly good for our @CPW11_ in Week 11 ( @awscloud ) pic.twitter.com/H8znETPdW2 — NFL Fantasy Football (@NFLFantasy) November 18, 2026 Will Parker Wahsington Have a Big Day Against the Giants in Week 11? Nov 5, 2026; Baltimore, Maryland, USA; Jacksonville Jaguars wide receiver Parker Washington (11) scores a touchdown in the second quarter against the Baltimore Ravens at M&T Bank Stadium. Mandatory Credit: James Lang-Imagn Images The 24-year-old Washington is having yet another strong season, which follows his breakout 2025 campaign. Last season, he put up a career-high 847 receiving yards to go along with five touchdowns on 58 catches and 95 targets. Through nine games this season, the former Penn State Nittany Lions star already has 645 receiving yards and six touchdowns (new career high) on 36 receptions and 64 targets. Washington is also coming off a stunning performance in Week 10’s 40-23 Jags win over the Tennessee Titans on the road, going off for 152 receiving yards and a touchdown on seven catches and nine targets. Washington will look to sustain that form when he takes on the Giants’ pass defense that is still formidable, one that is third overall in the league to date with just 184.1 passing yards allowed per outing. Aug 15, 2026; New Orleans, Louisiana, USA; Detailed view of the Jacksonville Jaguars helmet against New Orleans Saints during the first half at Caesars Superdome. item.title: Lewis Hamilton opens up on "isolating" feeling after seeing his own F1 Las Vegas grandstand
item.description: Motorsport photo Nearly two decades into his Formula 1 career, Lewis Hamilton still is not taking the scale of his following for granted. Speaking on media day ahead of the 2026 Las Vegas Grand Prix, the seven-time world champion offered a rare glimpse into the emotional toll of paddock life when asked what it meant to see fans packing his own dedicated grandstand at the circuit. "I never in a million years thought that, honestly, I never ever thought that I’d ever have my own grandstand," Hamilton said. "Also, I didn’t know that I would have such an amazing community of support that have kept me going all these years, and to see them here this weekend and in full force supporting... their energy makes the world of difference in a world that can sometimes be quite isolating and lonely, so it’s great when you get to see and share those experiences with a large group of people." Lewis Hamilton, Ferrari Lewis Hamilton, Ferrari The Lewis Hamilton Grandstand has returned to the Las Vegas Strip Circuit for a second consecutive season after debuting in 2025. Located near Turn 17 along the Harmon Straight inside The Performance Zone by WHOOP - formerly the West Harmon Zone - the stand has drawn heavy demand again in 2026, with Thursday and Friday single-day tickets already sold out on the official race portal. Organisers also expanded the package this year to grant ticket holders access across three fan zones, views of the F1 Academy paddock, and an exclusive Hamilton T-shirt for three-day buyers. Chasing a strong finish in the cold That support comes at a welcome point in a demanding campaign. Entering the season-closing triple-header across Las Vegas, Qatar, and Abu Dhabi, Hamilton is coming off a roller coaster Americas swing that saw him finish fourth in Austin and second in Mexico City before slipping to ninth in São Paulo. "It’s crazy to think it’s been such a long year, so I’m definitely looking forward to the end, but I’m also just wanting to try and see if we can finish on a high," Hamilton said. With Mercedes having already sealed both 2026 championships, Hamilton’s main target is protecting Ferrari ’s 95-point cushion over Red Bull for second in the constructors’ standings (510 points to 415). Individually, he enters Nevada fourth in the drivers’ table on 261 points—just one behind Mercedes’ George Russell and 18 adrift of Max Verstappen . Lewis Hamilton, Ferrari Lewis Hamilton, Ferrari "The main focus is making sure we solidify second in the constructors' [championship] for the team, because... it means a huge amount to everyone at the factory, but especially to me also," Hamilton said, adding that strong results could help him "climb back up from fourth and hopefully be in the top three". Improving on last year’s eighth-place finish in Vegas - after taking second in 2024 - will hinge on conquering the desert cold. "Getting the tyres working, that takes a lot of hard work from all the team, making sure we’ve got the tyres working in the right

item.title: Veteran righty pitches lights-out despite injury-plagued 2026
item.description: SAN DIEGO, CALIFORNIA - OCTOBER 06: Nick Pivetta #27 of the San Diego Padres pitches in the first inning against the Milwaukee Brewers in game three of the National League Division Series at Petco Park on October 06, 2026 in San Diego, California. (Photo by Orlando Ramirez/Getty Images) | Getty Images Welcome to our series grading every member of the San Diego Padres’ 40-man roster. The roster being evaluated is current as of Oct. 18, prior to the end of the World Series. Because of that, it will include players who will be free agents once the postseason concludes. Each player will be graded on their performance in the 2026 season, including the playoffs. That performance will be weighted based on how much time the player spent with the team (availability is the best ability). Nick Pivetta When the Padres signed Pivetta heading into the 2025 season, he was the last solid starting pitcher left on the free agent market. No other reliable options remained. San Diego signed him to a backloaded deal in order to maintain payroll flexibility. Pivetta turned in the best season of his career, earning some down-ballot Cy Young votes. He was expected to anchor the rotation alongside Michael King in 2026. Overall Grade: C- Things didn’t go according to plan. Pivetta made just four starts before hitting the injured list and remaining there for almost five months. He exited a start against the Colorado Rockies early and was later diagnosed with flexor strain in his throwing elbow. He ended up making just eight starts in total for the Friars due to several setbacks during his rehab assignments. But, when he was on the mound, it was a thing of beauty. Pivetta pitched to a 2.86 ERA in those eight starts (34.2 IP). He was even better after returning from the IL, posting a 1.45 ERA in the month of September. His overall ERA was only so high due to a rough Opening Day performance (6 ER, 3.0 IP). Removing that first outing, Pivetta holds a 1.42 ERA across 31 2/3 innings of work. He just didn’t pitch enough. The injury concerns led the Padres to decline his $14 million club option for the 2027 season. Reportedly, the two sides are still seeking a reunion. Had the Friars picked up Pivetta’s 2027 club option, he would have acquired an $18 million player option for 2028. San Diego probably didn’t want to be on the hook for that much if Pivetta’s arm gave out a second year in a row.

item.title: Cardinals’ Carson Beck Makes Notable Admission About His First NFL Start
item.description: Carson Beck finally got a taste of what it’s like to start a game in the pros after the Arizona Cardinals handed the rookie the keys to the offense in Week 10 against the Los Angeles Rams. Although Beck didn’t exactly shine in the Rams game, he had great things to say about the lead-up to that assignment against Myles Garrett and company. “I think that routine really helped and to be quite honest, like that was the most prepared I’ve ever felt for a football game in my life ever,” the former Miami Hurricanes star quarterback said talking to reporters on Wednesday. “So, it definitely helps that, you know, you’re able to be at the facility for, twelve, thirteen hours a day. But man, that’s that definitely props to, my coaches and, you know, how much time they spent just getting me ready and prepared for the game.” "To be quite honest, that's the most prepared I've ever felt for a football game in my life…ever." Carson Beck is confident in his coaches and preparation. pic.twitter.com/CQL0CqGMYy — PHNX Cardinals (@PHNX_Cardinals) November 18, 2026 Cardinals Rookie Beck Inherits QB1 Role Amid Interesting Turn of Events at Quarterback Nov 15, 2026; Glendale, Arizona, USA; Arizona Cardinals quarterback Carson Beck (19) warms up before the game against the Los Angeles Rams at State Farm Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Matt Kartozian-Imagn Images Beck becomes the Cardinals’ starting quarterback not entirely by design but partly out of necessity. Arizona started the season with Jacoby Brissett as its QB1. Several weeks later, he was replaced in favor of Gardner Minshew. Brissett was then traded to the Baltimore Ravens and Minshew is now done for the remainder of the season with an injury. That opened the door for Beck to take over the QB1 role for perhaps at least the rest of the campaign. Against the Rams, Beck went 11/18 for 108 passing yards and zero touchdowns. He was picked off twice and got sacked five times for a loss of 19 yards. It was quite a tough day for Beck, but he can get better with more reps. Beck will get another chance to impress on Sunday, albeit against another quality team in the form of the Kansas City Chiefs at Arrowhead Stadium in Kansas City. Nov 15, 2026; Glendale, Arizona, USA; Arizona Cardinals quarterback Carson Beck (19) looks to pass during the second quarter against the Los Angeles Rams at State Farm Stadium. Carson Beck is confident in his coaches and preparation. pic.twitter.com/CQL0CqGMYy — PHNX Cardinals (@PHNX_Cardinals) November 18, 2026 Cardinals Rookie Beck Inherits QB1 Role Amid Interesting Turn of Events at Quarterback Nov 15, 2026; Glendale, Arizona, USA; Arizona Cardinals quarterback Carson Beck (19) warms up before the game against the Los Angeles Rams at State Farm Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Matt Kartozian-Imagn Images Beck becomes the Cardinals’ starting quarterback not entirely by design but partly out of necessity. Arizona started the season with Jacoby Brissett as its QB1. Several weeks later, he was replaced in favor of Gardner Minshew. Brissett was then traded to the Baltimore Ravens and Minshew is now done for the remainder of the season with an injury. That opened the door for Beck to take over the QB1 role for perhaps at least the rest of the campaign. Against the Rams, Beck went 11/18 for 108 passing yards and zero touchdowns. He was picked off twice and got sacked five times for a loss of 19 yards. It was quite a tough day for Beck, but he can get better with more reps. Beck will get another chance to impress on Sunday, albeit against another quality team in the form of the Kansas City Chiefs at Arrowhead Stadium in Kansas City. item.title: Marlins, Angels Risk Top Prospects With Rule 5 Gamble
item.description: USA TODAY Network via Reuters Connect The Miami Marlins and Los Angeles Angels made bold moves this week by leaving high-value prospects unprotected ahead of the Rule 5 Draft deadline. While most teams rush to fill their 40-man rosters to keep players safe, these two clubs are betting that baseball will shut down before the draft ever happens. The contract talks between owners and players are stuck, with the current deal set to expire on December 1. If no new agreement is reached, the season goes into a lockout, and the draft gets cancelled. That is the gamble both front offices are taking right now. According to Just Baseball, the New York Mets set the tone for this strategy by protecting only their top prospect, Jefferson Rojas, and leaving the rest of their system exposed. if the draft never occurs, teams save valuable roster spots without losing talent. The Mets are hoping to keep two starting pitching prospects off the 40-man roster to stay flexible. This approach lets them avoid the rule that stops contact with players on the 40-man roster once the CBA expires. The Marlins and Angels are following this same playbook, but the risk is much higher for them. Marlins Leave Elite Arms Exposed The Miami Marlins added four players to their 40-man roster but chose to leave five ranked prospects open to selection. The most notable name they left behind is Karson Milbrandt, who is the club’s No. 6 overall prospect. Per MLB.com , Milbrandt earned a promotion to Triple-A after posting a 1.34 ERA at the Double-A level, but he struggled with an 8.39 ERA in his next 16 games. Despite the rough patch, he remains a top talent that other teams would love to steal for a full season. The Marlins also left infielder Brayden Taylor, the No. 10 prospect, and outfielder Kemp Alderman, the No. 8 prospect, off the protected list. By keeping these players off the 40-man, Miami hopes to maintain contact with them if a lockout hits. If the draft is cancelled, these players stay in the system for free. But if the draft goes on, the Marlins could lose Milbrandt or Taylor to another team that needs a bat or a pitcher. The risk is real because these players are close to the majors and have proven they can perform at high levels. The team is trading short-term safety for long-term roster flexibility, a move that only works if the league actually locks out the players. Angels Roll the Dice on Outfield Speed The Los Angeles Angels made similar choices by adding outfielders Nelson Rada and Raudi Rodriguez to the roster while leaving pitchers Mason McGwire and Joel Hurtado exposed. item.title: Barcelona superstar intent on reclaiming his place in Hansi Flick’s starting XI
item.description: Barcelona superstar intent on reclaiming his place in Hansi Flick’s starting XI Frenkie de Jong’s return from injury, although quite late, has served as a reminder for Barcelona as to why he is such a key player for the club. De Jong’s versatility has helped Barcelona navigate through an apparent injury crisis before the international break. This is despite the fact that De Jong was almost counted out by many, when Barça signed Rodri from Manchester City in the summer. De Jong ready to reclaim his place According to AS , De Jong is now prepared to go a step further and reclaim his regular starting role in the Barcelona first-team, as the club look to resume their campaign this weekend. De Jong has shown a lot of positivity since returning from injury. (Photo by David Ramos/Getty Images) As mentioned earlier, de Jong has already shown his commitment towards the team by playing in various roles, including as a right-back against Atletico Madrid and as a central defender against Alaves. He also played as an attacking midfielder against Real Madrid. Such kind of commitment came on the back of an ugly summer that saw him pick up an injury and returning to full fitness much later than initially expected. De Jong grew frustrated with his standing in the team during that time. But he is not keen on making a big fuss out of his situation and is ready to fight for his place in the team, in any way he can. That is part of the reason why the former Ajax sensation accepted the role of a right-back when Hansi Flick decided to start Marc Bernal in central midfield against Atletico Madrid. De Jong winning back the trust Can de Jong regain his place in the Barcelona starting eleven? (Photo by Alex Caparros/Getty Images) De Jong’s positive attitude hasn’t gone unnoticed by Barcleona fans, at the very least. His standing in the dressing room also remains high, with the midfielder even receiving praise from the new Netherlands coach Xavi Hernandez, who had given him the captaincy in the absence of Virgil van Dijk in the international break. While De Jong’s relationship with fans remains a love-hate affair, he was warmly received both against Alaves and on reaching 300 appearances for the club. De Jong remains strong and motivated, as he stated recently. He also rubbished claims of him refusing to play in last season’s UCL quarter-final against Atletico Madrid. Perhaps more importantly, his resurgence has led to calls of him starting together with Rodri and Pedri in midfield, though the chances of that remain slim. For now, De Jong will be focusing on getting back to full fitness for the Villarreal clash, though he has already received the green light to feature in that game.

item.title: Tyler Herro confirms what his relationship with Bam Adebayo is really like
item.description: Photo by Melissa Tamez/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images Tyler Herro hasn’t spoken to Bam Adebayo ahead of tonight’s matchup. Miami beat Milwaukee 137–130 on Wednesday night, and Bam Adebayo definitely got the upper hand on his old teammate. Adebayo put up 26 points, four rebounds, and two assists, while Tyler Herro had a rough night back in South Beach with just eight points and four assists on 4-of-11 shooting. Their seven-year run in Miami ended on ugly terms this past summer after Herro got shipped to the Bucks in the blockbuster Giannis Antetokounmpo trade. Leaked screenshots from an alleged burner account showed Herro trashing Adebayo’s contract and game, sparking a reported fight in Las Vegas, and the two didn’t interact once on Wednesday. Tyler Herro admits him and Bam Adebayo haven’t spoken Before tip-off against the Heat on Wednesday night, reporters asked Tyler Herro where things actually stand with Bam Adebayo after their messy summer fallout. His response: “I’m not sure. I mean, I haven’t talked to him. Obviously, spent a lot of time with Bam. I admire his game. He’s a great player. Can do everything on the floor. Guard one through five. Obviously, he’s gifted offensively, but I know how he’s wired. I know he’s a competitor, and I know how it’s going to be tonight, so I’m excited to just go up against everybody.” Tyler Herro and Bam Adebayo barely acknowledged each other all night. Right before tip-off, the old teammates stood just a couple of feet apart near the scorer’s table and made sure to look the other way. It was the exact same story after the final buzzer, as Adebayo dapped up a few Bucks players, walked right past Herro without a word, and headed straight to the locker room, leaving zero doubt about where things stand. item.title: Kick-off times and TV schedule revealed for Premier League’s January fixtures
item.description: The Premier League has revealed the kick-off times and TV schedule for its remaining January fixtures, with a number of huge match-ups moved into prime-time slots. Liverpool host Manchester United in Mauricio Pochettino’s first game as United boss this weekend and the reverse fixture between the two bitter rivals takes place in matchweek 22, with the game being moved into the Sky Sports slot at 4.30pm on Sunday 24 January. Earlier that day will have seen a London derby between Crystal Palace and Tottenham as one of four 2pm fixtures, while the previous day (Saturday 23 January) is headlined by Brighton vs Manchester City at 8pm on TNT Sports , with reigning champions Arsenal facing Newcastle at 5.30pm on Sky Sports that day. Mauricio Pochettino faces Liverpool in his Man United debut this weekend and again on Sunday 24 January (Getty) The following weekend is also a blockbuster, with the Merseyside derby kicking matchweek 23 off at 12.30pm on Saturday 30 January on TNT Sports, while Sky’s Super Sunday match is Man City vs Arsenal at 4.30pm. Brentford and Man United will round that weekend off at 8pm on Monday 1 February on Sky. Meanwhile matchweek 21 sees the rare occurrence of Arsenal, Man City, Liverpool and Chelsea all playing at 3pm on a Saturday (16 January) with Hull, Nottingham Forest, Crystal Palace and Sunderland the respective opponents. Aston Villa vs Man United is the 5.30pm clash that day, while Tottenham hosting Leeds headlines Sunday’s action at 4.30pm – with both those clashes on Sky Sports. Aston Villa v Man United will be at 5.30pm on Saturday 16 January (Getty) The Premier League also confirmed that the 2027/28 season will begin on Friday 13 August 2027 with the final round of fixtures being played on Sunday 21 May 2028 , with all 10 fixtures kicking off simultaneously in the normal manner. The start date gives 75 clear days from the end of the 2026/27 season, while the last day of the 27/28 campaign – which will consist of 33 weekends and five midweek match rounds in total – comes one week before the Champions League final. The Premier League also indicated that across Christmas and New Year, no two matchweeks will take place within 60 hours of each other to address the congested scheduled in the festive period. item.title: 'Cummins will struggle to captain Australia': Ian Healy's blunt warning after Bancroft's Sandpapergate revelations
item.description: Former Australia wicketkeeper Ian Healy has warned that Pat Cummins will struggle to lead the Test side unless he directly refutes Cameron Bancroft’s explosive claim that the entire team knew about the ball-tampering plan during the infamous 2018 Cape Town Test. Bancroft, one of the central figures in the Sandpapergate scandal, said on Tuesday that the entire team was aware of the conspiracy but he ended up taking "the bullet" for everyone. His remarks have reignited questions over what happened in South Africa and the credibility of those who maintained they knew nothing about the plot. The latest controversy follows Cummins dismissing former teammate Usman Khawaja's claim in his book that the entire team knew about the ball-tampering plan as “complete and utter nonsense.” Reacting to Bancroft's fresh allegations, Healy said Cummins needed to address the issue directly if he wanted to retain his authority as captain. "I would feel without refuting Cameron Bancroft's words again, he (Cummins) will struggle to captain the team. “You've had a big part of your credibility taken away with that press conference now that it's been proven to be not as complete as Pat made it out to be,” Healy told SEN. ALSO READ: Cummins under pressure as Bancroft's explosive claims trigger calls for captaincy review Healy says Cummins need not step down Asked whether Cummins should stand down as Australia captain, Healy said he did not believe that was necessary, while questioning the way Cricket Australia had handled the scandal in 2018. "No, he doesn't need to stand down. And I don't want to get into another panic mode of what happened in 2018, it was panic, and they tried to do an investigation in no time, didn't talk to anyone, it was rubbish. It was a lack of quality and rubbish, and rushed, and panicked. "Now, I can't say whether he should stand down now. Will he stand down? That might be a different thing. He might stand down," said the 62-year-old, who played 119 Tests and 168 ODIs between 1988 and 1999. Healy also argued that the latest revelations could damage the personal legacies of Cummins and fellow Australia bowlers Josh Hazlewood, Mitchell Starc and Nathan Lyon, who had said they were unaware of the ball-tampering plan. “I would say it taints their personal legacies. I don't think it's going to taint their performance legacies. Personally now, they're not as credible as they once were, unless they change something drastically in the next few days," Healy said. Healy also suggested that the ball-tampering could have been happening for longer than previously believed. “So they probably achieved some success with their skills, with a ball that's doing more than it was going to. That's a little bit of a part of their career legacy," he added. Healy calls for Lehmann to speak, rules out fresh probe Healy believes former Australia coach Darren Lehmann should now disclose what he knows about the scandal. "If he's going to do it, now's the time. But I think the dots have been joined there too. It was an ugly underbelly with an average attitude, and he was in charge of it,” Healy said. Healy also accused Cricket Australia of orchestrating a cover-up in the aftermath of the scandal, arguing that the panic following the events in South Africa resulted in a flawed investigation. “Yes, I think so...the panic and the chaos back here in Australia - they had no idea about it in South Africa - it was unbelievably emotional and led to a poor quality investigation which might have been covering up a motivation not to get everyone sacked," he said. item.title: 'Man of integrity' Diallo can restore proper values to FIFA: UEFA vice-president
item.description: French football chief Philippe Diallo (R) can restore values to FIFA that have been lost under the regime of Gianni Infantino (L), said a UEFA vice-president (FRANCK FIFE) French football chief Philippe Diallo's bid to depose Gianni Infantino as FIFA president is less about replacing one man than overhauling how football's governing body has been run under him, a UEFA vice-president told AFP. Laura McAllister, who in 2023 became the first woman to be elected a vice-president of European football's governing body, said Diallo was a "man of integrity" and his values aligned with UEFA "which it feels are critical to change the governance of FIFA". UEFA have been in the vanguard of opposition to Infantino -- they described his shortlived FIFA Forward Enterprise (FFE) plan to sell stakes in the World Cup to private investors as a "shabby, back room, opaque deal". McAllister said although some have dismissed Diallo as a stop-gap candidate, after others such as CONCACAF president Victor Montagliani and elder statesman Arsene Wenger opted out, he stood on his "merits". "We knew it would be a tricky process to find an appropriate candidate with regime change and accountability as the programme," she told AFP in a phone interview on Wednesday. "Philippe Diallo can do that adeptly. Were there other candidates mentioned before? Yes there were, but it is now about the timetable of aligning values and articulating them. "It does not matter about who might have been a candidate, this is the here and now and he is a strong and credible values-driven candidate." Diallo and former Japan Football Association president Kozo Tashima are hoping to dash Infantino's hopes of a fourth and final term in Rabat on March 18 next year. "We respect him a lot, his values align with ours," McAllister said of Tashima. "Let us see how that plays out." McAllister is at pains to insist it is more about changing the system than replacing one person. "It was never about ridding FIFA of one leader, it is about reform of the framework of governance, finance and redistribution system," she said. - 'Patterns of behaviour'- McAllister said Diallo, a 63-year-old lawyer whose Senegalese-born father boxed for France at an Olympics, should not be seen as solely a European candidate. "He is a francophone, which is an important asset in lots of CAF (Confederation of African Football) countries," she said. CAF have been among Infantino's most vocal supporters, partly because Morocco is co-hosting the 2030 men's World Cup. The South American governing body CONMEBOL also backs him. More surprising was the Asian Football Confederation's (AFC) volte-face -- having heavily criticised Infantino, they announced last month they supported his re-election. McAllister, a former captain of the Wales women's football team, noted though that confederations do not vote as a bloc.
