Laura McAllister, who in 2023 became the first woman to be elected a vice-president of European football's governing body, said Diallo was a "man of integrity" and his values aligned with UEFA "which it feels are critical to change the governance of FIFA". UEFA have been in the vanguard of opposition to Infantino -- they described his shortlived FIFA Forward Enterprise (FFE) plan to sell stakes in the World Cup to private investors as a "shabby, back room, opaque deal". McAllister said although some have dismissed Diallo as a stop-gap candidate, after others such as CONCACAF president Victor Montagliani and elder statesman Arsene Wenger opted out, he stood on his "merits". "We knew it would be a tricky process to find an appropriate candidate with regime change and accountability as the programme," she told AFP in a phone interview on Wednesday. "Philippe Diallo can do that adeptly. Were there other candidates mentioned before? Yes there were, but it is now about the timetable of aligning values and articulating them. "It does not matter about who might have been a candidate, this is the here and now and he is a strong and credible values-driven candidate." Diallo and former Japan Football Association president Kozo Tashima are hoping to dash Infantino's hopes of a fourth and final term in Rabat on March 18 next year. "We respect him a lot, his values align with ours," McAllister said of Tashima. "Let us see how that plays out." McAllister is at pains to insist it is more about changing the system than replacing one person. "It was never about ridding FIFA of one leader, it is about reform of the framework of governance, finance and redistribution system," she said. - 'Patterns of behaviour'- McAllister said Diallo, a 63-year-old lawyer whose Senegalese-born father boxed for France at an Olympics, should not be seen as solely a European candidate. "He is a francophone, which is an important asset in lots of CAF (Confederation of African Football) countries," she said. CAF have been among Infantino's most vocal supporters, partly because Morocco is co-hosting the 2030 men's World Cup. The South American governing body CONMEBOL also backs him. More surprising was the Asian Football Confederation's (AFC) volte-face -- having heavily criticised Infantino, they announced last month they supported his re-election. McAllister, a former captain of the Wales women's football team, noted though that confederations do not vote as a bloc. "There is a soft space which Philippe can exploit and convince some federations within each confederation to support a reform agenda," the 61-year-old said. "There is a lot of discomfort around the behaviour of Gianni Infantino and a desire to challenge the concentration of power in his hands. "This applies everywhere in world football. This is not about Europe, the same rules apply globally." McAllister, an academic who teaches governance at Cardiff University, said she believes the Asian confederation's values aligned with Diallo's. "His campaign will be a programme for change, modernising governance and accountability to who matters, as FIFA money belongs to associations, not any individual," she said. "The AFC and CONCACAF have aligned themselves with this agenda, for a president neither to operationally manage nor to intervene in decisions." Infantino looked odds-on to be re-elected unopposed after a highly successful staging of this year's World Cup, co-hosted by three countries for the first time. However, the revelations of his FFE plan changed the dynamic completely. "Patterns of behaviour stack up against him," McAllister said, detailing the incendiary FFE initiative but also the awarding of a FIFA Peace Prize to Donald Trump, which points to a perceived sycophancy towards world leaders. Then there was the introduction of hydration breaks at the World Cup and the decision to suspend a red card for USA forward Folarin Balogun at Trump's request. Some had hoped for a woman candidate. However, McAllister said the time was not right for either her or another vocal Infantino critic, Norwegian football chief Lise Klaveness. "I do not necessarily think the football world is ready for a reforming woman candidate, but it will be soon," she said. pi/gj

item.title: Woods to design new golf course in Northern Ireland
item.description: Woods said the new course is a special opportunity for his design firm [Getty Images] Tiger Woods is to design Northern Ireland's first new championship links golf course in more than a century. On Thursday, Woods and his course architecture firm TGR Design unveiled plans for Bellarena Golf Links on the Causeway Coast. The course will be located on Northern Ireland's northwest coast, about 20 miles west of three-time Open Championship venue Royal Portrush. Fifteen-time major champion Woods said the opportunity to create a new course in one of golf's most celebrated destinations was a special one. "Northern Ireland is home to some of the greatest links golf in the world, and building one on the Causeway Coast is a special opportunity for our team," said Woods. "We want Bellarena to feel as though it has always been part of this coastline, with a course that challenges the best players and is fun for everyone who plays it." The development, a partnership between Galgorm Collection and US-based Reef Destinations, is expected to break ground in 2027, subject to planning approval, with a target opening date of July 2029. "To have Tiger Woods and his company design a golf course in Northern Ireland is a once-in-a-lifetime opportunity, it's unbelievable," said Galgorm Collection chief executive Colin Johnston. "It's bringing together fantastic companies and partners and creating something that will benefit Northern Ireland for many years to come." Johnston said the dramatic setting was one of the key reasons the site stood out. "The backdrop of Binevenagh Mountain and the views over Lough Foyle and into the Donegal hills are just stunning," he said. The project could provide a boost to tourism in the north west. "We know golf tourism is huge and we know it's close to capacity," Johnston said. "If we want to bring more people to this part of the world, we need to increase that capacity, and it needs to be at the elite level people expect when they come here." Johnston believes Bellarena can complement Northern Ireland's world-renowned venues such as Royal Portrush and Royal County Down by helping attract new visitors. "This is about bringing something new and exciting to this part of the world, bringing more people here and increasing tourism overall," he added. Unlike some exclusive championship venues, Bellarena is expected to operate as a non-member, pay-and-play course. TGR has designed courses in the United States but Bellarena will be the firm's first project in Europe. Woods set to return next month after two years out

item.title: Chiefs News: Sunday is Travis Kelce’s 100th game at Arrowhead Stadium
item.description: (Photo by Amy Kontras/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Kansas City Chiefs have a lot of history with their home venue since 1972: Arrowhead Stadium. It has seen heartbreak and triumph over the years, and many loyal fans in Chiefs Kingdom have sat in the crowd over 100 times. However, only three Chiefs players have ever played in 100 regular-season games at Arrowhead — and tight end Travis Kelce is slated to be the fourth this Sunday. Chiefs Kingdom, bring the noise to the SB Nation app! Join fellow Chiefs fans to react to every explosive play and game-changing moment in real time. Chat live throughout the game Browse with fewer ads Easily jump between communities Enjoy faster commenting and posting Download the SB Nation app on iOS or Android . Download the SB Nation app on your mobile device! For Apple devices, click here . For Android devices, click here . The latest Kansas City Chiefs news Kansas City Chiefs tight end Travis Kelce’s top moments at Arrowhead Stadium | ESPN “You come through the facility, and you just see Arrowhead [Stadium] pop up out of nowhere,” Kelce said recently. “That’s the best feeling for me.” Few players in the Chiefs’ 67-year history have entered Arrowhead to put on the team’s red jersey, helmet and cleats as many times as Kelce. On Sunday, against the Arizona Cardinals (1 p.m. ET, CBS), Kelce will become only the fourth player in franchise history — joining Hall of Fame right guard Will Shields, kicker Nick Lowery and punter Dustin Colquitt — to play 100 regular-season games at Arrowhead, a venue that opened in 1972. Kelce considers Arrowhead a revered place, even before the venue was the site where his relationship with Taylor Swift, his wife, became public. Kansas City Chiefs share updated renderings of new stadium | KMBC 9 In another rendering, the interior of the stadium is shown, with, of course, a sea of red, and a domed roof. One rendering shows what the stadium could look like if Kansas City is selected to host the NCAA Final Four. In that rendering, a basketball court is shown in the middle of the stadium with fans covering the floor and the stands. The final design shows a first look at the possible entertainment district, with a paved walking area surrounded by restaurants and a Chiefs shop. Kansas City Chiefs vs. Arizona Cardinals Fantasy Football Matchup Breakdown For Week 11 | The Fantasy Life And oh yeah … start the Chiefs’ running back, whoever it may be. Backup Emmett Johnson did such an excellent job in relief (22-101-0; 6-70-2) that Andy Reid’s now granted the freedom to get Kenneth Walker as much time as he needs to heal up 100% for a deep playoff run. Crazy that Johnson’s logged a single start and still ranks as fantasy’s RB23 in total points — he’ll continue to rank as fantasy’s top backup with standalone value in games with double-digit spreads like this one, even if Walker suits up. Why Chiefs’ Emmett Johnson continues to tune out the noise despite recent success | The Kansas City Star Before

The latest Kansas City Chiefs news Kansas City Chiefs tight end Travis Kelce’s top moments at Arrowhead Stadium | ESPN “You come through the facility, and you just see Arrowhead [Stadium] pop up out of nowhere,” Kelce said recently. “That’s the best feeling for me.” Few players in the Chiefs’ 67-year history have entered Arrowhead to put on the team’s red jersey, helmet and cleats as many times as Kelce. On Sunday, against the Arizona Cardinals (1 p.m. ET, CBS), Kelce will become only the fourth player in franchise history — joining Hall of Fame right guard Will Shields, kicker Nick Lowery and punter Dustin Colquitt — to play 100 regular-season games at Arrowhead, a venue that opened in 1972. Kelce considers Arrowhead a revered place, even before the venue was the site where his relationship with Taylor Swift, his wife, became public. Kansas City Chiefs share updated renderings of new stadium | KMBC 9 In another rendering, the interior of the stadium is shown, with, of course, a sea of red, and a domed roof. One rendering shows what the stadium could look like if Kansas City is selected to host the NCAA Final Four. In that rendering, a basketball court is shown in the middle of the stadium with fans covering the floor and the stands. The final design shows a first look at the possible entertainment district, with a paved walking area surrounded by restaurants and a Chiefs shop. Kansas City Chiefs vs. Arizona Cardinals Fantasy Football Matchup Breakdown For Week 11 | The Fantasy Life And oh yeah … start the Chiefs’ running back, whoever it may be. Backup Emmett Johnson did such an excellent job in relief (22-101-0; 6-70-2) that Andy Reid’s now granted the freedom to get Kenneth Walker as much time as he needs to heal up 100% for a deep playoff run. Crazy that Johnson’s logged a single start and still ranks as fantasy’s RB23 in total points — he’ll continue to rank as fantasy’s top backup with standalone value in games with double-digit spreads like this one, even if Walker suits up. Why Chiefs’ Emmett Johnson continues to tune out the noise despite recent success | The Kansas City Star Before his junior season at Nebraska, Johnson said he was hearing “a lot of outside noise about what kind of year I would have and what I was capable of. My brother reminded me to ‘Tune Out the Noise.’” The quote comes courtesy of a clothing brand website started by the brothers — “Tune Out the Noise” — and explains the origin. TONT offers sweats, hoodies, T-shirts and hats emblazoned with an inspirational message about focusing on the task at hand. Chiefs terminate veteran LB, two-time Super Bowl champion in Week 11 | Chiefs Wire The Kansas City Chiefs terminated the practice squad contract of veteran linebacker Cole Christiansen on November 18. Christiansen started his career as an undrafted free agent with the Los Angeles Chargers in 2020 and signed with Kansas City in 2022. A member of the Chiefs’ Super Bowl LVII and LVIII rosters, Christiansen exclusively saw action as a special-teamer for Kansas City and Los Angeles, logging a total of 399 NFL snaps without a single defensive down played. Around the NF L Diego Pavia, Heisman finalist and former Vanderbilt star, picked No. 1 in UFL draft | The Athletic The Columbus Aviators picked the 24-year-old Pavia after his brief offseason stint in the NFL. Pavia went undrafted in April but later signed a three-year deal with the Baltimore Ravens. The Ravens, who have played four quarterbacks this season, waived Pavia in July to make room for center Ethan Pocic. At Vanderbilt, Pavia led the Commodores to their first 10-win season in 2025 and became the school’s first Heisman Trophy finalist. He finished second in voting to Indiana’s Fernando Mendoza, the eventual No. 1 pick in the 2026 NFL Draft. Cowboys’ Mike Pettine to take over defensive play-calling duties from DC Christian Parker | NFL.com Pettine has been a coordinator with the New York Jets, Buffalo Bills and Green Bay Packers. He also served as head coach of the Cleveland Browns from 2014 to 2015. The Cowboys will keep the 34-year-old Parker in the defensive coordinator role, but hope putting play-calling in the hands of the more experienced Pettine will help turn around a defense that has been torched in 2026. Parker is “a critical piece of what we’re trying to do as we search for answers and solutions,” Cowboys coach Brian Schottenheimer said Wednesday, confirming the decision. “I think he has an incredibly bright future not just this year but beyond with us. Cam Skattebo says he is retiring his backflip celebration after what happened to Aidan Hutchinson | Yahoo! Sports “It’s hard to see,” Skattebo told a couple of reporters after Monday’s practice. “I’m saying yeah (no more). Mentally, I’m like, ‘I’m not doing that.’ That ain’t going to happen to me.” Skattebo has become known for his backflip celebration. Even after dislocating his ankle and fracturing his tibia last year, he was seen still sporting his backflip celebration at a Fanatics Fest event over the summer that sent social media into a frenzy. While head coach John Harbaugh and general manager Joe Schoen spoke with him after that event, Skattebo said this decision to retire his backflip is his alone. In case you missed it on Arrowhead Pride Andy Reid and Chiefs will be cautious with Kenneth Walker this week It would feel shortsighted for the Chiefs to put Walker on the field against the (3-7) Arizona Cardinals in a game where Kansas City is favored by 15.5 points, according to FanDuel Sportsbook . Four days after that matchup, the Chiefs will be on the road to play their AFC rivals, the (8-1) Buffalo Bills, in a pivotal Thanksgiving night game. Reid acknowledged that the quick turnaround could factor into Walker’s availability this weekend. “That goes into the equation,” Reid said about the coming short week. “I’m not saying that’s the answer, but that goes into [it]. You look at the distance between games, you look at what the symptoms are and where he’s at.” “If he’s not going to further injure it, then he’ll go play,” Reid stated. “If he can, if it looks like he’s on the edge there, then he doesn’t play. Keep it simple.” From The Feed Follow Arrowhead Pride on Social Media Facebook: Like our page Instagram: @ArrowheadPride X: Follow @ArrowheadPride AP Staff on X: See complete list

item.title: Julius Randle Rips Nets Teammates After 30-Point Loss To Bulls: “That Was Embarrassing”
item.description: Mandatory Credit: Jordan Godfree-Imagn Images The Brooklyn Nets ‘ 2026-27 season went from bad to worse on Wednesday, as the Chicago Bulls blew them out 137-107 at Barclays Center. The Nets trailed by as many as 37 points against the lowly Bulls, and Julius Randle’s frustrations got the better of him at one point. With the Nets en route to an embarrassing defeat, Randle was seen going off on his teammates for having no pride during a timeout. Sat behind the bench.. new team low. Julius Randle tells the team there’s no pride — crisper (@botcrisps) November 19, 2026 Both teams entered this game with 3-10 records, but the Nets made the Bulls look like one of the best teams in the NBA. Randle was asked postgame what their main struggle was and how the game got away from them, and he did not hold back. “The main struggle?” Randle asked, via Chaz NBA. “I don’t know, that was embarrassing. Been in the league for 13 years, and that’s one of the worst games I’ve ever been a part of, and not because of the score. You lose by 30 sometimes; it’s just a bad night, but it’s how we did it. It just wasn’t cool. “Nothing about it was cool,” Randle added. “And we got to find a way to figure out the root of it or whatever, but that just unacceptable.” The Nets actually kept pace with the Bulls early on, but then collapsed. The visitors ended the first quarter on a 13-0 run to take a 37-21 lead and never looked back. The Bulls ended up making a franchise-record 15 three-pointers in the first half and led 76-51 at the break. What made this performance all the more embarrassing was that the Nets were honoring members of their 1974 and 1976 ABA championship-winning teams at halftime. The great Julius Erving was among those in attendance and saw the team lay an egg. Randle had a team-high 15 points at halftime and finished the game with 17 points (5-10 FG), four assists, and one steal. The 31-year-old was asked postgame about getting heated at his Nets teammates. “Just a little frustrated,” Randle said. “It was tough. And like I said, I’ve been in the league for 13 years, and it just felt like five individuals out there. And I was just trying to somehow, someway relay to the group that winning is the most important thing, not individuals. So we got to find a way to get connected as a group and put that first. But I have to be better; I have to find a way to be better. Like I said, I put it on me.” Randle, acquired from the Minnesota Timberwolves this past offseason, is one of the two notable veterans on this Nets team, along with Michael Porter Jr. They have to do better as leaders. “I’m always going to hold myself accountable and figure out ways or find ways to do more,” Randle said. “Yeah, I think, you win, you find ways to win. When you lose, you find excuses. It seems like a lot of excuses. So for me, I got to go back into work. I got to go back into the film. I got to figure. I got to look myself in the mirror tonight, too, like everybody else, and figure out what

Fernandez will hope that happens when they take on the Orlando Magic at Barclays Center on Friday at 7:30 p.m. ET. That’s an Emirates NBA Cup game as well, and another defeat would all but end their hopes of advancing to the knockout stage.

item.title: 76ers provide an update on star guard following hamstring injury
item.description: 76ers provide an update on star guard following hamstring injury originally appeared on The Sporting News . Add The Sporting News as a Preferred Source by clicking here . The Philadelphia 76ers have gotten off to a red-hot start to the season, posting a 13-3 record that sees them sit at the top of the Eastern Conference standings. This shouldn't come as too much of a surprise, given that all of their top talents have been firing on all cylinders, with Tyrese Maxey, Joel Embiid, and Jaylen Brown all averaging 20 points or more. But Wednesday night's win over the Orlando Magic saw them overcome a new challenge in the season: a stacked injury report. Philadelphia was without the aforementioned Maxey and Brown, which could cause some concern for the Sixers faithful, but for Maxey, there isn't much to worry about. Nick Nurse said Tyrese Maxey and Dean Wade were held out mostly out of precaution. Maxey went through shootaround this morning, but his foot began bothering him pregame. Just wanted to hold him out for this one. #Sixers — Ky Carlin (@Ky_Carlin) November 19, 2026 According to USA Today's Ky Carlin, the Sixers' coach stated that the two-time All-Star was held out of the match just as a precaution. Brown to undergo further tests However, according to Carlin , the prognosis for Brown's hamstring strain that kept him out of Wednesday night's match will have to wait a little longer, as the team will re-evaluate him when they return from their road trip. "He’s gonna get re-evaluated when we get back home," Carlin wrote, quoting the aforementioned Nurse. "So. just know he's out tonight and we'll look at him when we get back." Given that Philadelphia has two days off ahead of their NBA Cup match against the Milwaukee Bucks on Saturday night, all eyes will be on the results of the tests for Brown's injury. The five-time All-Star has been one of the more lethal parts of Philadelphia's offensive arsenal, averaging 22.6 points and 6.6 rebounds per night, while shooting 49.4 percent from the field. The Philadelphia 76ers have gotten off to a red-hot start to the season, posting a 13-3 record that sees them sit at the top of the Eastern Conference standings. This shouldn't come as too much of a surprise, given that all of their top talents have been firing on all cylinders, with Tyrese Maxey, Joel Embiid, and Jaylen Brown all averaging 20 points or more. But Wednesday night's win over the Orlando Magic saw them overcome a new challenge in the season: a stacked injury report. Philadelphia was without the aforementioned Maxey and Brown, which could cause some concern for the Sixers faithful, but for Maxey, there isn't much to worry about. Nick Nurse said Tyrese Maxey and Dean Wade were held out mostly out of precaution. Maxey went through shootaround this morning, but his foot began bothering him pregame. Just wanted to hold him out for this one. #Sixers — Ky Carlin (@Ky_Carlin) November 19, 2026 According to USA Today's Ky Carlin, the Sixers' coach stated that the two-time All-Star was held out of the match just as a precaution. Brown to undergo further tests However, according to Carlin , the prognosis for Brown's hamstring strain that kept him out of Wednesday night's match will have to wait a little longer, as the team will re-evaluate him when they return from their road trip. "He’s gonna get re-evaluated when we get back home," Carlin wrote, quoting the aforementioned Nurse. "So. just know he's out tonight and we'll look at him when we get back." Given that Philadelphia has two days off ahead of their NBA Cup match against the Milwaukee Bucks on Saturday night, all eyes will be on the results of the tests for Brown's injury. The five-time All-Star has been one of the more lethal parts of Philadelphia's offensive arsenal, averaging 22.6 points and 6.6 rebounds per night, while shooting 49.4 percent from the field. More Sixers news: Sixers' Tyrese Maxey puts league on notice with recent post Sixers' Tyrese Maxey named to All-NBA third team Did the Sixers just find their Jared McCain replacement? 76ers decline team option on veteran forward following rough season 76ers opt to bring back standout forward after impressive season 76ers' Free Agency Primer: What do they need?

item.title: How a restoration added challenge to Sea Island without changing its soul
item.description: ST. SIMONS ISLAND, Ga. – For years, longtime Sea Island instructor Jack Lumpkin carried around a list of places where he believed the Seaside Course could be lengthened. “Whenever anybody would listen, he'd take us out there and show us, ‘You should back this tee up,’” Davis Love III recalled. Lumpkin passed away several years ago, but his vision has finally become reality. Ahead of this week's RSM Classic, Sea Island unveiled a multi-million-dollar restoration of its famed Seaside Course led by Love Golf Design, headed by Love, his brother, Mark, and lead architect Scott Sherman, in collaboration with MacCurrach Golf Construction. The project was designed to honor the course's architectural heritage while enhancing playability for resort guests and adding subtle challenge for tournament competitors. Originally designed by Harry Colt and Charles Alison in 1929, the Seaside Course underwent a major renovation in 1999 when Tom Fazio combined nine holes from the original Alison layout and nine from a Joe Lee-designed course to create an entirely new 18-hole design. The latest restoration included a complete turf replacement, infrastructure upgrades, dune restoration and a series of strategic refinements throughout the property. “We used historic pictures and Google Earth as a guide to restore Tom Fazio's original vision,” Love said. Among the changes are new back tees on Nos. 5, 6, 7, 9, 11, 13, 15 and 16, adding roughly 150 yards to the par-70 layout, which now stretches to 7,157 yards. Many of those additions trace directly to suggestions Lumpkin championed for years. The project also included installation of a new irrigation system. The greens remain TifEagle Bermudagrass, while the collars, approaches, tees, fairways and rough were converted to Platinum Paspalum, a grass variety prized for its salt tolerance in coastal environments. Some of the most significant architectural changes came on the back nine. At the par-4 10th hole, the green was moved approximately 20 yards farther from the tee and lowered about two feet, with its original contours preserved through digital scanning technology. The par-4 15th also received a substantial makeover. A new back tee lengthened the hole, while the green was shifted closer to the water and lowered slightly. The left greenside bunker was eliminated, creating a wider approach area between the water hazard and the lone bunker on the right. “I think the second shot on 15 is way more exciting and consequential than it was before,” said Maverick McNealy, whose lone career win on the PGA Tour thus far came at the 2024 RSM Classic. I think there's going to be a lot more variance in score because of the water bringing in on the left," said veteran Tour pro Keith Mitchell, a local resident. SIMONS ISLAND, Ga. – For years, longtime Sea Island instructor Jack Lumpkin carried around a list of places where he believed the Seaside Course could be lengthened. “Whenever anybody would listen, he'd take us out there and show us, ‘You should back this tee up,’” Davis Love III recalled. Lumpkin passed away several years ago, but his vision has finally become reality. Ahead of this week's RSM Classic, Sea Island unveiled a multi-million-dollar restoration of its famed Seaside Course led by Love Golf Design, headed by Love, his brother, Mark, and lead architect Scott Sherman, in collaboration with MacCurrach Golf Construction. The project was designed to honor the course's architectural heritage while enhancing playability for resort guests and adding subtle challenge for tournament competitors. Originally designed by Harry Colt and Charles Alison in 1929, the Seaside Course underwent a major renovation in 1999 when Tom Fazio combined nine holes from the original Alison layout and nine from a Joe Lee-designed course to create an entirely new 18-hole design. The latest restoration included a complete turf replacement, infrastructure upgrades, dune restoration and a series of strategic refinements throughout the property. “We used historic pictures and Google Earth as a guide to restore Tom Fazio's original vision,” Love said. Among the changes are new back tees on Nos. 5, 6, 7, 9, 11, 13, 15 and 16, adding roughly 150 yards to the par-70 layout, which now stretches to 7,157 yards. Many of those additions trace directly to suggestions Lumpkin championed for years. The project also included installation of a new irrigation system. The greens remain TifEagle Bermudagrass, while the collars, approaches, tees, fairways and rough were converted to Platinum Paspalum, a grass variety prized for its salt tolerance in coastal environments. Some of the most significant architectural changes came on the back nine. At the par-4 10th hole, the green was moved approximately 20 yards farther from the tee and lowered about two feet, with its original contours preserved through digital scanning technology. The par-4 15th also received a substantial makeover. A new back tee lengthened the hole, while the green was shifted closer to the water and lowered slightly. The left greenside bunker was eliminated, creating a wider approach area between the water hazard and the lone bunker on the right. “I think the second shot on 15 is way more exciting and consequential than it was before,” said Maverick McNealy, whose lone career win on the PGA Tour thus far came at the 2024 RSM Classic. I think there's going to be a lot more variance in score because of the water bringing in on the left," said veteran Tour pro Keith Mitchell, a local resident. "I think you'll still see some eagles and birdies, but I think you'll start to see some higher scores as well." Despite the extensive scope of the project, the objective was not to dramatically alter one of the PGA Tour's most recognizable venues. “I think every golf course that Davis touches is fantastic. The stuff he did at Plantation is amazing. The changes he made at Sawgrass, at Harbour Town are fantastic,” McNealy said. “We were saying in the locker room if you hadn't played here in six years, you might not know there's much of a difference.” That sentiment may be the ultimate measure of success for the restoration: a course that looks much the same to players and fans, but one that now more closely reflects both Fazio's original intent and Lumpkin's long-held vision. Adam Schupak is a senior writer for Golfweek, covering the PGA Tour. This article originally appeared on Golfweek: How a restoration added challenge to Sea Island without changing its soul

item.title: Emi Martinez backs Como star Nico Paz to take over Lionel Messi’s iconic Argentina No. 10 jersey
item.description: Argentina v Costa Rica - International Friendly - Getty Images Sport Chelsea goalkeeper Emiliano Martinez believes Como standout Nico Paz has the potential to inherit Lionel Messi's iconic No. 10 shirt for Argentina. The young midfielder recently scored a brace against Costa Rica, sparking intense debate about his future international role. Martinez backs Paz for iconic shirt Martinez believes Paz has the quality to become Argentina's next No. 10. The debate over who will inherit the legendary jersey has intensified following Messi's international retirement . Paz thrust himself into the spotlight on Tuesday by scoring a brace in Argentina's emphatic 7-0 victory over Costa Rica . The Como midfielder has now registered a remarkable five goals in his last five appearances for the national team. His rapid emergence has made him a highly credible candidate to step into the playmaking void. Senior players within the Argentina setup are already throwing their support behind the youngster. Building the Argentine fighting spirit Martinez, a key figure in the Argentina dressing room, has expressed immense confidence in the midfielder's potential. The goalkeeper revealed that the squad is actively nurturing the Como star to prepare him for the biggest stages. "I see him becoming more and more integrated into the group," the Chelsea player admitted, as quoted by Mundo Deportivo . "Obviously, he needs to have that Argentine fighting spirit, and we’re helping him develop it. The truth is, he deserves everything that’s happening to him right now. He deserves to be here and to play. The goals he’s scoring are an added bonus." Embracing the ultimate national responsibility Taking over the primary creative role for Argentina comes with immense pressure, but Martinez feels Paz possesses the correct mindset. The veteran believes humility will be the defining factor in the youngster's long-term success. "If he maintains this humility and keeps performing at this level, Nico Paz can definitely wear Argentina’s No. 10 shirt and take on that responsibility," Martinez added. "We need players like him, players who see themselves as leaders. He can help us win a lot of games. We have to help him. We’re a national team. There are no egos here. It’s all about hard work, humility, and respect." Shining bright in Italy and beyond Paz is currently enjoying a remarkable rise at club level, having just started his third season with Como. During the previous campaign, he was instrumental in helping Cesc Fabregas' team secure Champions League qualification for the first time in their history. That impressive form has seamlessly carried over into the 2026-27 season. The dynamic midfielder has already racked up six goals and eight assists in just 14 appearances across all competitions for the Italian club.

item.title: Hamilton picks Verstappen as target for hilarious cheese bazooka attack
item.description: Lewis Hamilton has jokingly named Max Verstappen as the Formula 1 driver he would target with a giant cheese bazooka, following an unusual question from fans during an event in Las Vegas. While the media have been asking drivers more serious questions about their performances, the championship battle and the challenges awaiting them at the Las Vegas Grand Prix , fans have taken a rather different approach, putting Hamilton on the spot with a particularly bizarre question. The seven-time world champion was taking part in a fan event ahead of the Las Vegas Grand Prix when he was presented with a rather unconventional scenario involving a hypothetical weapon fitted to his Ferrari steering wheel. Asked which driver he would shoot if he had a button capable of firing melted cheese from a giant bazooka, Hamilton initially struggled to settle on a name. "That's a really good question. Who should I blast with cheese? That's pretty funny," the Ferrari driver responded. After someone suggested that a particular driver was already on his mind, Hamilton insisted he was still undecided and turned to the audience for suggestions. "No, I don't know who to pick. Who do you all think would be good?" Photo: Race Pictures Photo: Race Pictures Hamilton rules out Leclerc before settling on Verstappen Verstappen was the first name suggested by the crowd, prompting an amused reaction from Hamilton. "Verstappen?" he repeated, laughing, before asking: "Anyone else?" Another fan proposed Charles Leclerc, but Hamilton immediately ruled out targeting his Ferrari teammate, explaining that their shared responsibilities on the track should take priority. "He's my teammate. I can't say my teammate. We have to win as a team," Hamilton replied. The Briton then floated Lando Norris as another possible target, before someone in the audience suggested Nico Hulkenberg. However, Hamilton was unwilling to pick the German, describing him as harmless. "Nico's harmless. Everyone's saying Max, so maybe I'll go with that. He's probably the closest, so let's cover Max in cheese."

item.title: 2 Newcastle players ruled out of Arsenal clash
item.description: 2 Newcastle players ruled out of Arsenal clash Newcastle United will be without a couple of players for Arsenal’s visit on Saturday, but the vast majority of their players are expected to be fit. Photo by Stu Forster/Getty Images Newcastle United are expected to have one significant injury absentee for Arsenal’s visit to St. James’ Park this weekend, with Joelinton set to miss the match. Joelinton missed Newcastle’s last game against Fulham with a thigh issue,, and there was some initial uncertainty around exactly how long he’d be out. But Lee Ryder confirms for The Journal that the player has at least been ruled out of the Arsenal fixture. Newcastle will also be without backup goalkeeper Ewen Jaouen , but that’s unlikely to have a material impact on the result. The 20-year-old is still waiting on his Premier League debut. Photo by Ed Sykes/Getty Images Then former Arsenal player Joe Willock and ex-Manchester City midfielder Nico Gonzalez were both missing from training earlier this week due to illness, but the duo are expected to return in time for the weekend fixture. So in terms of potential starters, Joelinton is the only player who won’t be available to Newcastle boss Matthias Jaissle . Arsenal are obviously in a relatively similar situation, with Bukayo Saka the only confirmed injury absentee for the match. But Max Dowman will also be missing through the final game of his suspension, Martin Zubimendi is a doubt, and William Saliba is still yet to play any first-team minutes after injury. Photo via Arsenal.com Zubimendi is Arsenal’s one new injury concern from the international break, with the majority of the squad appearing to come through their games without any setbacks. There was some concern about Christos Tzolis mid-break, as he complained of muscle pain and was sent for an MRI. But the results came back all-clear, and he ended up playing Greece’s next game. Photo by Dean Mouhtaropoulos/Getty Images 2 Newcastle players ruled out of Arsenal clashNewcastle United will be without a couple of players for Arsenal’s visit on Saturday, but the vast majority of their players are expected to be fit. item.title: Parents: please don’t buy Grand Theft Auto VI for your child
item.description: Rockstar Games’ brilliant 18-rated criminal caper is stuffed with sex, drugs and violence. It is the most explicit game I’ve ever played – and it really is not for kids I am haunted still by an interaction I had at my stepson’s ninth birthday party in 2014, where one of the kids asked if I could put on Grand Theft Auto V for them all. “I have it at home!”, he said, giving me the puppy-dog eyes. Mentally replaying that game in my head, flashing back to the many scenes involving such things as smoking meth, over-the-top gratuitous violence and grubby sex in one character’s trailer, I said “ no way” . Later I gently mentioned to the kid’s mother that GTA V was an 18-rated game and really wasn’t suitable for kids. “Oh, but he’s really good at these games,” she told me. She was genuinely shocked to learn that an 18-rating on a video game was a flag for adult content, rather than an indication of its difficulty. Grand Theft Auto VI is released this week. It is an incredible creative and technical feat, conjuring a realistic-looking and exhaustively detailed virtual Florida filled with every kind of filth and criminality you could imagine. It is brilliant, entertainingly observed and even sometimes unexpectedly touching, largely thanks to a central love story between the player couple , Jason and Lucia. It is lewd, violent and frequently hilarious. It is also absolutely full of stuff that I really would not want my 10 and seven-year-old boys to see or hear. I have never played a game that has more thoroughly earned its 18 rating. Continue reading...

Talking trade We start with the trade inside the top five, with the New York Jets moving up to No. 2 to draft Drew Mestemaker from Oklahoma State. There are a few things to discuss when it comes to this hypothetical. The Jets are loaded with three picks in the first round, but if they want to draft the quarterback at the top of their board, they will likely have to move ahead of the Miami Dolphins at No. 3. With picks No. 4 and No. 13, they can do just that, while retaining a pick at No. 6 (courtesy of the Indianapolis Colts and the Sauce Gardner trade) to address another position of need. In this scenario that is Notre Dame cornerback Leonard Moore. But … trading up for a quarterback prospect who did not even start for his high school team and is just in his first year as a starter for a Power 4 school? There is a lot to like about Mestemaker, from his ability in the downfield passing game, his athleticism, his willingness to challenge tough windows over the middle, and his touch when layering throws to all levels of the field. But in many ways it is that fact, that he is wrapping up his first year as a starter at a Power 4 school, that works in his favor. The trajectory is impressive and the upside is off the charts. I was a fan of his after last year , and have only grown more impressed with his profile. As for the Chargers’ side of this trade, they get a new target for Justin Herbert in Charlie Becker out of Indiana, and Ashton Hampton to address a need in the secondary. Where is Arch Manning? This is likely the next big question: Where is Arch Manning? Sitting here on the cusp of Thanksgiving, I’m not sure Manning enters the draft. His game against LSU — much like his games against Ole Miss and Ohio State earlier this season — was another microcosm of his current draft profile: Some great moments late, overshadowing some difficult moments earlier. Now, maybe Manning does enter the draft, and if he does it will be interesting to see how the greater draft community stacks him with the rest of this class. But right now, I think it is more likely he heads back to Texas, or even entertains the transfer portal, than he heads to the NFL. What about the rest of the quarterbacks? Now let’s talk about the rest of the quarterbacks … both those listed here and two names that are not. We can start with the two quarterbacks not listed here in this first-round mock: Austin Simmons and Trinidad Chambliss. Beginning with Simmons, much like Manning I think he heads back to Missouri for another season. Simmons recently signed a new deal with the school for 2027 , but he does have an option to enter the NFL Draft. But with the Tigers’ recent slide, I think it is likely he heads back to campus with that new deal in hand, to try and make another run. As for Chambliss, as much as I like him, I do wonder if the NFL will view him the same way that I do. He might slide to the top of the second round, which will not be a bad thing for him. That leaves Dante Moore as the next quarterback off the board, to the Cleveland Browns. While Deshaun Watson has stabilized that position this season, Cleveland still needs a long-term solution, and Moore was a potential top-five pick a year ago, and the talent is there. Then we get CJ Carr to the Minnesota Vikings at the end of the first round. I think he would be a good fit for Kevin O’Connell, and it sets up a scenario where yet again Kirk Cousins could be mentoring a first-round pick. This idea sent me down the road of a “Mandalorian” world where Cousins just mentors a first-round pick to start each season before moving on to a team making a surprise playoff run despite a glaring need at the position. A hired gun, spaghetti Western style, year after year. I’ve said to much. But you know where to find me Netflix. A running back in the top 10? I know, I know … But the more I thought about pairing Jaden Baugh with the Houston Texans, the more sense it made. And one does not need to look far for inspiration. Take the Kansas City Chiefs, who stabilized their running game with the addition of Kenneth Walker III this past offseason. Walker has given Kansas City an explosive element in the run game, and put the Chiefs back among the AFC’s list of elite teams. For a team like the Texans, bolstering the running attack makes a world of sense. While part of it is game-script dependent, Houston ranks 29th in the league in rushing yards per game , and 24th in Expected Points Added per Rush. Going offensive line here is also an option for Houston but Baugh, who is explosive both on the ground and through the air, is a fun fit for them.

item.title: 'I feel like we're in an Orwell novel right now': Joel Klatt slams CFP selection committee
item.description: Credit: Steve Roberts-Imagn Images, The Joel Klatt Show We got another look at the College Football Playoff selection committee’s rankings on Tuesday, and there is once again plenty to talk about . While there were a few eyebrow-raising decisions across the top 25 — four ranked four-loss SEC teams, Arizona moving up four spots with a loss, Indiana at No. 8 after its shuffling last week — the biggest question mark by a pretty wide margin was the committee’s ranking of No. 3 Alabama relative to No. 5 Texas. There was no great move here, as Alabama held serve at No. 3 with a comfortable win over Vanderbilt, while Texas moved up one spot following its on-the-road win over No. 21 LSU. Instead, it was the lack of movement that was the real news. After the Hoosiers got punished during their bye week, presumably as a result of several of their previous wins taking losses while they were off, many expected the same to happen for the Crimson Tide this week, as Alabama’s five best wins this season all lost this past week. Instead, the committee remained unshaken in its faith in Bama. Joel Klatt, who has never been shy about sharing his opinions on the committee’s rankings, did not hold back while breaking down what he saw as an insult to college football fans. “I feel like we’re in an Orwell novel right now,” Klatt said on Wednesday. “The committee is basically insisting we reject the evidence right before our eyes. Right in front of our faces. It is like their most essential command. “I see the resume between Alabama and Texas. Two spots behind Alabama is Texas, and Texas’ resume is so much better than Alabama’s. Their best wins, Bama, are now Kentucky and South Carolina, who just got the hinges blown off of their front door by Arkansas. … Texas beat Tennessee and Ohio State. A Tennessee team that beat Alabama. There’s no comparing those two resumes. You took a wrong turn, you’re telling us it’s a shortcut, and now you’re just stubborn. Take the crayons away from the committee.” Klatt then imagined a conversation he’d have with a defender of the committee’s current ranking, pointing out the circular reasoning of those that argue in favor of the SEC’s ranked four-loss teams. “The Tide looked very average. ‘Yeah, but hey, it was in the SEC.’ Well, why is that good? ‘Well, because nine teams are ranked.’ Yeah, but why were nine teams ranked? ‘Well, because the SEC is really good.’ Why is the SEC really good? ‘Well, because nine teams are ranked.’ Oh! See I didn’t get it the first time. Thank you for clarifying. “None of it makes sense. They’re asking us to suspend all of our faculties and just believe what they give us, and I refuse to do that.” Take the crayons away from the committee. https://t.co/0sBVAfEvtx — The Joel Klatt Show: A College Football on FOX Pod (@JoelKlattShow) November 18, 2026 The weekly ceremony of the rankings show is starting to get pretty exhausting, as the committee’s logic can sometimes fail to add up in a way that makes sense from w

item.title: Brewers captain Christian Yelich leaves fans speechless with unexpected visits
item.description: Milwaukee Brewers captain Christian Yelich is finding new ways to celebrate the team’s first World Series championship, this time by surprising fans with unexpected deliveries. A Fanatics video shared Tuesday, nearly three weeks after Milwaukee secured the title, shows the veteran taking part in the gesture. The company also credited UPS for helping make the surprises possible and tagged Yelich in its caption. Ayyy Christian Yelich just surprised fans after winning a RING Shoutout @UPS for hooking it up @ChristianYelich pic.twitter.com/lfr1OjAfl8 — Fanatics (@Fanatics) November 17, 2026 One Brewers fan is shown reacting in disbelief, exclaiming, “Oh my god” after an unexpected visit from the Brewers star. The clip highlights the excitement surrounding Yelich’s surprise appearances. Fanatics posted the footage on X (formerly Twitter), on Tuesday, showing how the veteran helped extend Milwaukee’s championship festivities directly to fans’ homes. Christian Yelich visiting Brewers fans’ homes Oct 28, 2026; St. Petersburg, Florida, USA; Milwaukee Brewers designated hitter Christian Yelich (22) celebrates in the clubhouse after defeating the Tampa Bay Rays in game five of the 2026 World Series at Tropicana Field. Mandatory Credit: Kim Klement Neitzel-Imagn Images Fanatics did not disclose what the packages contained, who received them or where the deliveries took place. Its mention of Yelich earning a ring refers to Milwaukee’s World Series victory and does not establish that fans received championship rings. The surprises came after Yelich made several public appearances to celebrate the Brewers’ first title, secured with a five-game series win over the Tampa Bay Rays. The Brewers sealed the championship with a 4-1 victory in the decisive game at Tropicana Field, bringing the Commissioner’s Trophy back to Wisconsin after their postseason run. Yelich had taken on the captaincy shortly before the playoffs , with the team announcing his appointment during the final weekend of the regular season. Oct 12, 2026; Milwaukee, Wisconsin, USA; Milwaukee Brewers designated hitter Christian Yelich (22) hits a two RBI single against the Los Angeles Dodgers during the third inning in game two of the NLCS for the 2026 MLB Playoffs at American Family Field. Mandatory Credit: Benny Sieu-Imagn Images The latest clip showed Yelich celebrating the title in a different way by bringing the excitement straight to individual supporters. With Fanatics and UPS helping organize the drop-offs, unsuspecting Brewers fans got an unexpected visit from their team captain instead of seeing him at a traditional championship event. item.title: Every player from California to play for the Boston Celtics
item.description: The Boston Celtics have traded for, signed, and drafted players from nearly every U.S. state and countries across the globe. From Alabama to Yugoslavia, the Celtics have a history of thoroughly seeking talent to succeed in the NBA. Since their beginnings in the Basketball Association of America (a precursor league of the NBA) in the earliest years of the Association, the organization has tirelessly searched for talent since its inception. In this installment of our series documenting the origins of every player who has represented the Celtics, we will focus on players from California who have played for Boston. Our focus in this article is Malik Fitts. An alum of Saint Mary's, he went unselected in the 2020 NBA Draft, playing in other leagues until he signed with the Utah Jazz in 2021. The Lynwood, California native signed with the Celtics in 2022. His stay with the team lasted until he was traded to the Indiana Pacers that summer. item.title: China, US, Russia issue ‘peace declaration’ after first summit
item.description: China, the United States and Russia issued a “peace declaration” Thursday following an unprecedented leaders’ summit, almost five years into the Ukraine war and with Donald Trump bogged down in Iran. The statement after Xi Jinping, Trump and Vladimir Putin met in China, said that they wanted to reform the United Nations, to protect diplomatic immunity and boost supply and production of refined petroleum products. “The three heads of state engaged in an in-depth exchange of views on the current international situation and committed themselves to upholding strategic stability and international security,” said the statement published by Chinese state media and the Kremlin, but not yet by the White House. The three-way meeting took place with Russia’s years-long offensive in Ukraine grinding on, mayhem in the Middle East in the wake of Trump’s attacks on Iran, and an ascendant China looking to strengthen its hand in East Asia. “Our countries have many converging interests when it comes to resolving regional conflicts, including, of course, the conflict in Ukraine,” Putin said at the start of the meeting, adding they had a “shared responsibility for maintaining international peace and security”. The three men made opening remarks touching on weighty topics from nuclear weapons to the war in Ukraine as they met around a large, dark round table with a pink flower arrangement at its centre. The discussion behind closed doors in Kylin Villa in Shenzhen ended after an hour and 20 minutes. Trump said the three men were “making history”, while Putin said they wrote a new “page in the history of diplomacy”. “The three countries share a common perspective on safeguarding world peace,” Xi said. ICC, UN and oil In their joint statement, the leaders agreed that “the International Criminal Court and other similar institutions must not abuse their jurisdiction.” Putin is subject to an ICC arrest warrant while Trump’s administration has vowed to dismantle the court “brick by brick”. The leaders also “acknowledged the vital importance of the principle of state consent and the respect for (diplomatic) immunity enjoyed by state officials”, the statement said, adding that each country was “committed” to advancing the reform of the United Nations. Putin said the discussion would also touch on food and energy security – both of which have been upended by conflicts in Iran and Ukraine. The joint statement said the countries “plan to increase the production and supply of refined petroleum products”, reaffirming “the importance of the stable flow of energy”. The summit stoked fears that the three powerful men want to divide the globe into spheres of influence, for example by making decisions impacting Ukraine over the heads of Kyiv or Europe. item.dc:creator: Oboh
item.content:encoded: China, the United States and Russia issued a “peace declaration” Thursday following an unprecedented leaders’ summit, almost five years into the Ukraine war and with Donald Trump bogged down in Iran. The statement after Xi Jinping, Trump and Vladimir Putin met in China, said that they wanted to reform the United Nations, to protect diplomatic immunity and boost supply and production of refined petroleum products. “The three heads of state engaged in an in-depth exchange of views on the current international situation and committed themselves to upholding strategic stability and international security,” said the statement published by Chinese state media and the Kremlin, but not yet by the White House. The three-way meeting took place with Russia’s years-long offensive in Ukraine grinding on, mayhem in the Middle East in the wake of Trump’s attacks on Iran, and an ascendant China looking to strengthen its hand in East Asia. “Our countries have many converging interests when it comes to resolving regional conflicts, including, of course, the conflict in Ukraine,” Putin said at the start of the meeting, adding they had a “shared responsibility for maintaining international peace and security”. The three men made opening remarks touching on weighty topics from nuclear weapons to the war in Ukraine as they met around a large, dark round table with a pink flower arrangement at its centre. The discussion behind closed doors in Kylin Villa in Shenzhen ended after an hour and 20 minutes. Trump said the three men were “making history”, while Putin said they wrote a new “page in the history of diplomacy”. “The three countries share a common perspective on safeguarding world peace,” Xi said. ICC, UN and oil In their joint statement, the leaders agreed that “the International Criminal Court and other similar institutions must not abuse their jurisdiction.” Putin is subject to an ICC arrest warrant while Trump’s administration has vowed to dismantle the court “brick by brick”. The leaders also “acknowledged the vital importance of the principle of state consent and the respect for (diplomatic) immunity enjoyed by state officials”, the statement said, adding that each country was “committed” to advancing the reform of the United Nations. Putin said the discussion would also touch on food and energy security – both of which have been upended by conflicts in Iran and Ukraine. The joint statement said the countries “plan to increase the production and supply of refined petroleum products”, reaffirming “the importance of the stable flow of energy”. The summit stoked fears that the three powerful men want to divide the globe into spheres of influence, for example by making decisions impacting Ukraine over the heads of Kyiv or Europe. Earlier Thursday, Trump and Putin held a meeting — their first since August 2025 — with the 80-year-old US president calling the Russian his “friend”, who responded in English: “Nice to meet you.” Trump and Xi then came together – for the third time this year – for one-on-one discussions, with the US leader highlighting their “very special relationship”. Putin, 74, and Xi, 73, held talks on Wednesday – their 50th meeting, the Chinese president said. ‘Cheap violin’ Beijing, Washington and Moscow previously gave different accounts of the agenda for the three-way meeting on the sidelines of the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) summit, a forum of 21 economies around the Pacific rim. Washington initially signalled that Ukraine was off the table, before Trump said the war would feature. Xi does not view the conflict as China’s problem to solve. Critics warned that the optics from the meeting would be damaging for the US president — but a fillip to Xi and Putin. The meeting “gives Putin a platform to legitimise his war of aggression over Ukraine with seemingly little repercussions,” said Lyle Morris at the Asia Society Policy Institute. “Xi Jinping and Vladimir Putin are playing Donald Trump like a cheap violin,” Senate Democratic leader Chuck Schumer said. Washington had also flagged up the Iran war and nuclear disarmament as topics of discussion, after a US-Russia bilateral treaty on atomic weapons expired in February. Beijing has long maintained that the United States and Russia must reduce their giant nuclear arsenals before it agrees to talks on its smaller stockpile. The final statement said that the “three nations will engage in dialogue on reducing nuclear risks and preventing nuclear proliferation”. The extraordinary meeting preceded equally unusual scenes as the leaders arrived in the southern Chinese city for the talks. Breaking with decades of diplomatic protocol, Xi received Trump at the airport, with the men briefly hugging before a red-carpet greeting complete with cheering children and an air force flyover. Despite their differences, all the leaders – including Putin – posed for the APEC “family photo” on Thursday in special scarves. item.title: I let Apple’s always-listening AI summarize my life for two weeks
item.description: Siri Recap can be turned on or off manually from the wrist. Was it worth it? I've been asking myself this quite a bit over the last month or so while testing both the Amazon Bee Frontier and Siri Recap on the Apple Watch Ultra 4. Both enable a wearable to ambiently listen to your conversations and, using AI, summarize them for you. Why? So you can remember better and, hopefully, stay more present. The main difference is that Amazon's Bee takes a maximalist (and frankly reality-bending) approach, whereas Apple is going for a more minimalist, privacy-first take. Both, however, require explicit disclosures to the people around you about recording what they say, and potentially follow-up explanations a … Read the full story at The Verge.

item.title: National Automation Prize 2026 Unveils Shortlisted Innovators For Nigeria’s First Innovation Reality Tv Competition
item.description: The organizers of the National Automation Prize (NAP) 2026 , Advanxis Technologies & Process Automation Ltd., are pleased to announce the successful shortlisted candidates for the third edition of the prestigious national engineering and technology competition. Following a review of applications received from innovators, students, engineering professionals, universities, polytechnics and research institutions across Nigeria, outstanding projects have been selected to advance to the next stage of the competition. NAP 2026 is set to make history as Nigeria’s first innovation-focused reality television competition , bringing engineering creativity, industrial automation, artificial intelligence and robotics into the national spotlight. One of NAP Previous Winners SHORTLISTED CANDIDATES The successful applicants have been selected under two categories: 1. Individual Category Featuring outstanding innovators, students, engineers and technology enthusiasts developing practical solutions to real-world challenges. INDIVIDUAL CATEGORY — 40 QUALIFIERS NAP 2026 Individual shortlist 2. Institutional Category Featuring qualifying teams from universities, polytechnics and research institutions presenting innovative engineering and automation projects. INSTITUTION CATEGORY — 20 QUALIFIERS NAP 2026 Institution shortlist NEXT STAGE: REGIONAL AUDITIONS The shortlisted candidates will proceed to the regional auditions commencing 23 November 2026 , ahead of the highly anticipated national finale in Lagos. The grand finale programme will commence on 13 December 2026 , featuring a one-week innovation reality TV experience involving technical challenges, project demonstrations, mentorship, teamwork and competitive engineering activities. The competition will culminate in a spectacular Grand Finale and Awards Ceremony on 19 December 2026 , hosted by veteran Nollywood actor Emeka Ike . Veteran Nollywood Actor Emeka Ike NAP 2026 Host With over ₦50 million in prizes and technical development support , NAP 2026 aims to identify, celebrate and empower Nigeria’s next generation of engineering innovators. Speaking on the initiative, the organizers reaffirmed their commitment to bridging the gap between education, innovation and industry while promoting indigenous technological solutions. “Build for Nigeria. Automate for Scale. Compete with the World.” All shortlisted candidates are encouraged to monitor official communication channels for further instructions regarding regional auditions and participation requirements. For media enquiries and further information: Lagos: 16 Karimu Katun Street, Victoria Island, Lagos Port Harcourt: 22 Trans Amadi Road, Trans Amadi, Port Harcourt, Rivers State info@advanxis.com • +234 816 005 2942 • www.advanxis.com/prize3 The post National Automation Prize 2026 Unveils Shortlisted Innovators For Nigeria’s First Innovation Reality Tv Competition appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: FIFA chief Infantino faces challenge from France’s Diallo, Japan’s Tashima
item.description: French football chief Philippe Diallo and veteran Japanese official Kozo Tashima were on Thursday confirmed by FIFA as the challengers to incumbent Gianni Infantino in next year’s presidential election. Infantino has faced criticism over his aborted plan to allow private investment into the World Cup, but he retains considerable support for his bid to win re-election next March. French Football Federation president Diallo will represent UEFA, the European confederation which has been the most vocal in its criticism of Infantino. Tashima is a former head of the Japan Football Association and has served on the FIFA Council. FIFA said the candidacies will be examined by the body’s electoral committee before a final decision is made on whether to admit them. Ramon Vega, the Swiss former Tottenham defender who had expressed a desire to run against Infantino, was not included among the candidates. Diallo has indicated he would like to hold talks with Tashima, with a view to “joining forces” to unseat Infantino. The 68-year-old Japanese official, who has said he wants to make FIFA a “more trusted organisation”, said he was open to talks but was cautious about the steps after that. “It’s clear we need to talk,” Tashima told French sports daily L’Equipe on Wednesday. “But we must consider one thing: is the mere fact that our programmes are similar, enough for us to decide to work together, or unite? Or should we think tactically, asking what the most effective strategy would be to defeat Infantino?” In opposing Infantino, Tashima is going against his own confederation after the Asian Football Confederation (AFC) announced last month that it would support the 56-year-old Swiss for re-election. Infantino also has the backing of the Confederation of African Football (CAF), while South American governing body CONMEBOL is largely supportive. Under his rule, FIFA’s profits have skyrocketed and so have the amounts that member federations receive. The post FIFA chief Infantino faces challenge from France’s Diallo, Japan’s Tashima appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: Middle Belt youth leader rejects Tinubu’s 2027 endorsement, backs Obi
item.description: By Golok Nanmwa JOS — The National Youth Leader of the Middle Belt Forum (MBF), Emmanuel Zopmal, has rejected the purported endorsement of President Bola Tinubu for re-election in 2027 by some Middle Belt leaders, declaring support for the presidential ambition of the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC) candidate, Peter Obi, and his running mate, Rabiu Kwankwaso. Zopmal, who is also the North-Central Coordinator of The Big-Tent Coalition, stated this on Thursday while addressing journalists in Jos, Plateau State, where he presented the position of the Middle Belt youth leadership on the political future of the region. He faulted the reported endorsement, alleging that it did not reflect the collective position of the people because critical stakeholders, including community leaders, traditional institutions, youths and women, were not consulted before the visit to the President. “There was no due consultation with Middle Belt communities, elders, traditional institutions, youths and women who feel and live the terrible experiences in our various communities before the purported endorsement of President Tinubu for the 2027 re-election bid,” he said. Zopmal described the reported endorsement as insensitive to the security and economic challenges confronting communities across the region and the country. He cited insecurity, economic hardship, inflation, rising borrowings and poverty as issues that should have informed any political position taken in the name of the Middle Belt. The MBF youth leader also questioned the leadership and administrative structure of the forum, alleging that it had operated without a General Assembly, elections, constitutional processes and accountability for eight years. He called for the organisation to return to democratic principles and provide clearer direction for the Middle Belt struggle. He also criticised the immediate past President of the forum, Dr Pogu Bitrus, over what he described as a lack of broad-based consultations in the organisation’s activities. “We believe that no individual or group should assume the authority to speak for the entire Middle Belt without the consent and participation of the people and the various structures of the Forum,” he said. item.dc:creator: Nwafor
item.content:encoded: By Golok Nanmwa JOS — The National Youth Leader of the Middle Belt Forum (MBF), Emmanuel Zopmal, has rejected the purported endorsement of President Bola Tinubu for re-election in 2027 by some Middle Belt leaders, declaring support for the presidential ambition of the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC) candidate, Peter Obi, and his running mate, Rabiu Kwankwaso. Zopmal, who is also the North-Central Coordinator of The Big-Tent Coalition, stated this on Thursday while addressing journalists in Jos, Plateau State, where he presented the position of the Middle Belt youth leadership on the political future of the region. He faulted the reported endorsement, alleging that it did not reflect the collective position of the people because critical stakeholders, including community leaders, traditional institutions, youths and women, were not consulted before the visit to the President. “There was no due consultation with Middle Belt communities, elders, traditional institutions, youths and women who feel and live the terrible experiences in our various communities before the purported endorsement of President Tinubu for the 2027 re-election bid,” he said. Zopmal described the reported endorsement as insensitive to the security and economic challenges confronting communities across the region and the country. He cited insecurity, economic hardship, inflation, rising borrowings and poverty as issues that should have informed any political position taken in the name of the Middle Belt. The MBF youth leader also questioned the leadership and administrative structure of the forum, alleging that it had operated without a General Assembly, elections, constitutional processes and accountability for eight years. He called for the organisation to return to democratic principles and provide clearer direction for the Middle Belt struggle. He also criticised the immediate past President of the forum, Dr Pogu Bitrus, over what he described as a lack of broad-based consultations in the organisation’s activities. “We believe that no individual or group should assume the authority to speak for the entire Middle Belt without the consent and participation of the people and the various structures of the Forum,” he said. On the recent visit by some Middle Belt leaders to Tinubu, which involved elder statesman and retired General Theophilus Danjuma, Zopmal alleged that the exercise was influenced by the political interests of some individuals. He expressed concern that the outcome of the meeting could be wrongly associated with Danjuma’s position without the wider consent of the people. Zopmal further argued that the Middle Belt Forum should remain non-partisan, questioning why representatives of opposition parties from the region were excluded from the engagement. “Middle Belt Forum is not a partisan platform. We have Middle Belters who are national chairmen of other major opposition political parties. Why were they not involved in the visit, while the APC National Chairman was in attendance?” he queried. He also dismissed reports suggesting that a Middle Belt candidate could be considered for the All Progressives Congress (APC) presidential ticket in 2031, saying such assurances were not sufficient grounds for supporting Tinubu’s re-election. “Middle Belt people should not be persuaded to support a political project on the basis of promises about what may happen in 2031. Our immediate concerns are security, economic empowerment, justice and the welfare of our people,” he said. Appealing to Danjuma to reconsider the reported endorsement, Zopmal said the region needed concrete commitments on security and development rather than political assurances. “We want to appeal to our father, Gen. T.Y. Danjuma, to reconsider the purported endorsement. The future of the Middle Belt is too important to be determined without the involvement of the people,” he stated. He also accused the Federal Government of failing to do enough to address the plight of communities affected by violent attacks, particularly the resettlement of internally displaced persons (IDPs) and restoration of livelihoods. “None of our grabbed community lands has been recovered. No IDPs have been resettled to their ancestral homeland,” he alleged. He further claimed that there was no sustainable government programme to rebuild affected communities or a clear plan to enable residents return to their farms without fear. Zopmal also criticised the President’s handling of security challenges in Plateau State, particularly the Palm Sunday attack, arguing that affected communities required more visible government intervention. He said Plateau and other Middle Belt communities deserved sustained government attention, protection and concrete measures to address the consequences of violent attacks. Declaring support for Obi and Kwankwaso ahead of the 2027 presidential election, Zopmal said his coalition would mobilise voters across the region for the NDC candidates. “Peter Obi is the only presidential candidate who has consistently identified with the Middle Belt struggle, visited troubled communities and supported families affected by violent attacks. We believe his engagement with the region reflects the values of justice, fairness and equity,” he said. He called on youths and women across the region to participate actively in the electoral process, vote according to their conscience and resist inducements. He also urged them to defend their votes and ensure their voices count in the democratic process. Zopmal said the Middle Belt struggle remained anchored on justice, fairness and equity, adding that the coalition would continue to mobilise support for what it described as a more inclusive and accountable Nigeria. The post Middle Belt youth leader rejects Tinubu’s 2027 endorsement, backs Obi appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: Video: Fresh protest hits South Africa as demonstrators demand ban on Nigerians
item.description: By Ayobami Okerinde A fresh anti-Nigerian protest has erupted in South Africa, with demonstrators in Pretoria demanding that the government close its borders to Nigerian nationals and prohibit their entry into the country. The demonstration, organised by the March and March movement on Wednesday, saw protesters accuse Nigerians of involvement in drug trafficking and worsening social problems in South African communities. In a video shared by South African broadcaster, Newzroom Afrika, the group’s leader, Jacinta Ngobese-Zuma, was seen leading demonstrators through Sunnyside, a Pretoria suburb with a sizeable Nigerian population, popularly nicknamed ‘Little Lagos’. Video: Fresh protest hits South Africa as demonstrators demand ban on Nigerians Led by Jacinta Ngobese-Zuma, the protesters say the 1951 Refugee Convention is not sustainable and feasible, and South Africa should get out of it. pic.twitter.com/5nam29TgCL — Vanguard Newspapers (@vanguardngrnews) November 19, 2026 Addressing Nigerians in the neighbourhood, Ngobese-Zuma questioned how the area acquired the nickname and challenged residents to explain their presence in the community. “I am being told here that we’ve entered Sunnyside, the home of Nigerians. I am inviting Nigerians to come out, let’s talk to each other. We want to know who gave you this place and called it Nigeria. Who gave you permission to call this place Lagos or whatever you call it?” she said. She also described the presence of migrants in the country as unsustainable, alleging that they were putting pressure on public resources and contributing to the difficulties faced by South African citizens. The group’s legal representative, Xolani Zuma, also called for a blanket ban on Nigerians entering South Africa, accusing them of selling drugs to South Africans. “The state must ban Nigerians from South Africa. They must ban Nigerians until they stop selling drugs to our people. The rest of Africa, we are fine, but we do not want Nigerians in South Africa anymore. That is what we are saying,” he said. Speaking in another video, Ngobese-Zuma urged the South African government to withdraw from the 1951 United Nations Convention Relating to the Status of Refugees, arguing that its obligations under the agreement were no longer sustainable. “We need to get out of it, it’s not sustainable or feasible,” she said. The post Video: Fresh protest hits South Africa as demonstrators demand ban on Nigerians appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: From Tunde Kelani to Akinola Davies Jr., 5 Nollywood Directors You Should Know
item.description: From music visuals to international festival stages and actor-turned-director debuts, Dammy Twitch, Akinola Davies Jr., and Daniel Etim Effiong represent different paths into Nollywood directing. Think about the Nigerian films and series you have watched recently, the ones that kept you glued to your screen, had you talking about the storyline long after the credits rolled or recommending them to everyone you know. While the actors are often the faces you remember first, there is someone behind the camera whose creative choices help bring those stories to life: the director. From interpreting the script and guiding actors to shaping how each scene looks, sounds and unfolds, directors influence almost every part of what ends up on screen. As Nollywood grows in ambition, production quality and global reach, the filmmakers steering these projects are becoming just as central to the industry’s story as the stars in front of the lens. Some have spent decades bringing Nigerian literature and history to the screen, while others are earning international acclaim or crossing over from music videos into feature films. Here are five Nollywood directors whose work is worth knowing. Tunde Kelani Start with Tunde Kelani if you want to see where modern Nigerian cinema found its literary and cultural roots. Trained at the London Film School after cutting his teeth in photography and television, the Mainframe Films founder has spent decades turning Nigerian literature, stage plays, and history into lasting screen works. Titles like Ti Oluwa Nile , Koseegbe , O Le Ku , Saworoide , Thunderbolt: Magun , The Narrow Path , Maami , Dazzling Mirage , Ayinla , and Cordelia show how wide his range goes. Across years of festivals and awards, Kelani has collected major honours for his craft, and his adaptation Cordelia earned him a Best Director nomination at the 2026 Africa Magic Viewers’ Choice Awards. Tunde Kelani, whose directing catalogue spans Ti Oluwa Nile, Saworoide, The Narrow Path, Maami, and Cordelia, with Kunle Afolayan outdoors. Photo Credit: Tunde Kelani/Instagram Akinola Davies Jr. Few directors have linked global festival stages with homegrown Nollywood triumphs quite like Akinola Davies Jr. After his short film Lizard won the Short Film Grand Jury Prize at the Sundance Film Festival in 2021, he co-wrote and directed his feature debut My Father’s Shadow alongside his brother Wale Davies . The drama made history in 2025 as the first Nigerian film selected for the Official Selection at the Cannes Film Festival, picking up a Special Mention for the Caméra d’Or before winning Best Director at the British Independent Film Awards and Breakthrough Director at the Gotham Independent Film Awards. His momentum rolled straight into 2026 with a BAFTA win for Outstanding Debut by a British Writer, Director or Producer, followed by Best Director and Best Overall Movie wins at the 2026 AMVCAs. Akinola Davies Jr. with his BAFTA trophy for My Father’s Shadow. Photo Credit: A

Photo Credit: Tunde Kelani/Instagram Akinola Davies Jr. Few directors have linked global festival stages with homegrown Nollywood triumphs quite like Akinola Davies Jr. After his short film Lizard won the Short Film Grand Jury Prize at the Sundance Film Festival in 2021, he co-wrote and directed his feature debut My Father’s Shadow alongside his brother Wale Davies .
